tour-eiffel.name: Eiffel Tower
descriptions: It was built for the 1889 World's Fair
It was supposed to be dismantled after 20 years
It grows about 15 cm in summer due to the heat
It was the tallest monument in the world for 41 years
It's the most-visited paid monument in the world

notre-dame-paris.name: Notre-Dame de Paris
descriptions: Its construction took nearly two centuries
It welcomes 13 million visitors each year
The 2019 fire destroyed its famous spire
Victor Hugo dedicated a novel to it in 1831
Its restoration involves craftsmen from around the world

chateau-versailles.name: Palace of Versailles
descriptions: The palace has 2,300 rooms
The gardens cover 800 hectares
Louis XIV moved his court there in 1682
The Hall of Mirrors is 73 meters long
30,000 workers were needed to build it

louvre.name: Louvre Museum
descriptions: It's the most-visited museum in the world
It displays more than 35,000 works of art
The glass pyramid was inaugurated in 1989
The building was originally a medieval fortress
The Mona Lisa is protected by bulletproof glass

arc-de-triomphe.name: Arc de Triomphe
descriptions: It honors the soldiers who died for France
The Flame of the Unknown Soldier burns continuously
Its top offers a view over twelve star-shaped avenues
Napoleon never saw it finished in his lifetime
It stands 50 meters tall and 45 meters wide

mont-saint-michel.name: Mont-Saint-Michel
descriptions: The abbey is built on a granite islet
The tide can rise as fast as a galloping horse
It's been connected to the mainland by a footbridge since 2014
It's one of the most-visited sites in France
More than 300 people live there year-round

sacre-coeur.name: Sacré-Cœur Basilica
descriptions: It's built on top of Montmartre hill
Its construction was funded by national subscription
Its dome reaches 83 meters high
Its white stones self-clean in the rain
It was completed after the Franco-Prussian War of 1870

pont-du-gard.name: Pont du Gard
descriptions: It carries water 50 km from Uzès
Built without mortar, the blocks hold by their own weight
It stands 49 meters tall
It's the tallest preserved Roman aqueduct in the world
It carried 40,000 cubic meters of water per day

palais-des-papes.name: Palais des Papes
descriptions: It's the largest medieval Gothic palace in the world
Nine popes lived there between 1309 and 1377
Its stone walls are 4 meters thick
It hosts theater festivals every summer
It was used as a prison and barracks after the Revolution

cite-de-carcassonne.name: Cité de Carcassonne
descriptions: Its ramparts stretch over 3 kilometers
The city has 52 defensive towers
It was extensively restored by Viollet-le-Duc in the 19th century
It served as a film set for Pays de Cocagne

chateau-chantilly.name: Château de Chantilly
descriptions: Its museum holds the largest painting collection in France after the Louvre
The Great Stables could house 240 horses
Whipped Chantilly cream is said to have been invented there
It was partly demolished during the Revolution
The Duke of Aumale donated it to the Institut de France

opera-garnier.name: Palais Garnier
descriptions: Charles Garnier was only 35 years old when he won the competition
The chandelier in the main hall weighs 8 tons
It inspired the novel The Phantom of the Opera
Beneath the building lies a real underground lake
It has 17 stages and 6 floors of sets

colisee.name: Colosseum
descriptions: It could hold 50,000 to 80,000 spectators
Its construction took only 10 years
Gladiators didn't fight lions in every match
A system of awnings (velarium) shielded it from the sun
It served as a stone quarry for centuries

saint-pierre-rome.name: St. Peter's Basilica
descriptions: It's the largest church in the Christian world
Its dome was designed by Michelangelo
The square can hold 300,000 people
Its construction took 120 years
It's built on the supposed tomb of Saint Peter

pantheon-rome.name: Pantheon
descriptions: Its 43-meter concrete dome has stood intact for 2,000 years
The oculus at the top is the only source of natural light
Roman gods were worshipped there all together
Raphael is buried there
Its rotunda has inspired hundreds of buildings worldwide

tour-de-pise.name: Leaning Tower of Pisa
descriptions: Its construction lasted nearly 200 years
It tilts 3.97 degrees after partial straightening
Galileo is said to have tested gravity by dropping objects from it
Soft clay soil caused its lean
It's part of the UNESCO-listed Piazza dei Miracoli

palais-des-doges.name: Doge's Palace
descriptions: It was the home of the Doges of Venice for 1,000 years
The Bridge of Sighs connects the palace to the prisons
It holds some of the largest Tintoretto paintings in the world
Its pink facade is made of Verona marble
The last Doge left the palace in 1797

duomo-florence.name: Florence Cathedral
descriptions: Its dome is the largest brick dome in the world
Brunelleschi invented a special machine to build it
The dome weighs about 37,000 tons
There's no external scaffolding visible from the city
The interior decoration is deliberately simple

chateau-saint-ange.name: Castel Sant'Angelo
descriptions: It was originally built as Emperor Hadrian's mausoleum
A secret passage connects it to the Vatican
It has been a fortress, prison, and papal residence
Archangel Michael gave it its name in the 6th century
It overlooks the Tiber and the Via della Conciliazione

forum-romain.name: Roman Forum
descriptions: It was the political and commercial heart of ancient Rome
It was rediscovered under meters of earth in the 19th century
The Sacred Way ran through it from the Colosseum to the Capitol
It holds the remains of the Temple of Saturn from 497 BCE

trevi.name: Trevi Fountain
descriptions: It's the largest Baroque fountain in Rome
Over one million euros in coins are tossed in each year
It marks the end of a restored Roman aqueduct
Fellini's film La Dolce Vita made it famous worldwide
It's continuously fed by the Aqua Virgo aqueduct

milan-duomo.name: Milan Cathedral
descriptions: Its construction took nearly 600 years
It has 135 spires and 3,400 outdoor statues
The Madonnina statue at the top is 4.16 meters tall
It's the largest Gothic cathedral in Italy
Its rooftop is open to the public by stairs or elevator

pompei.name: Pompeii
descriptions: The city was buried under 6 meters of ash in 79 CE
Excavations began in 1748 under Charles III
Plaster casts reveal the postures of victims
More than two-thirds of the site has been excavated
About 15,000 to 20,000 people lived there

pont-du-rialto.name: Rialto Bridge
descriptions: It's the oldest bridge over Venice's Grand Canal
It was built in stone after wooden bridges collapsed
It has held jewelry shops since it was built
Its single arch spans 28 meters
Two staircase ramps flank its shopping galleries

basilique-saint-marc.name: St Mark's Basilica
descriptions: Saint Mark's relics were brought there from Alexandria in 828
Its facade is covered with over 8,000 m² of mosaics
The four bronze horses on the portal came from Constantinople
It long served as the Doge's private chapel
Its mosaic floor depicts symbolic animals

scala-milan.name: La Scala
descriptions: It opened in 1778 with a work by Salieri
Its orchestra pit can hold 100 musicians
The main hall seats more than 2,000 spectators
Verdi, Puccini and Toscanini all started or triumphed there
It was destroyed by bombings in 1943 and then rebuilt

arc-constantin.name: Arch of Constantine
descriptions: It's the largest preserved Roman triumphal arch
It was built to celebrate Constantine's victory over Maxentius
It mixes sculptures from different imperial eras
It directly inspired the Arc de Triomphe in Paris
It stands 21 meters tall and 25 meters wide

big-ben.name: Big Ben
descriptions: Big Ben originally referred to the great bell, not the tower
The tower has officially been called Elizabeth Tower since 2012
The bell weighs 13.5 tons
The clock mechanism has been running since 1859
Its slight tilt to the northwest is 0.26 degrees

tower-bridge.name: Tower Bridge
descriptions: Its two Gothic towers hide a steel structure inside
The central deck can lift in 90 seconds
It opens about 800 times a year for large ships
It was inaugurated by the Prince of Wales in 1894
A glass walkway at the top offers a view straight down

stonehenge.name: Stonehenge
descriptions: The largest stones weigh up to 25 tons
The bluestones come from Wales, 250 km away
Its construction spread over 1,500 years
It's perfectly aligned with the summer solstice
Its religious or astronomical use is still debated

buckingham-palace.name: Buckingham Palace
descriptions: It has 775 rooms, including 92 offices and 78 bathrooms
The royal flag shows whether the sovereign is in residence
The palace is surrounded by a 16-hectare garden
The balcony was added in 1851 for royal appearances
It only became the official residence in 1837 under Victoria

tour-de-londres.name: Tower of London
descriptions: William the Conqueror had it built to control the city
The Crown Jewels are kept and displayed there
Ravens are kept there because of a royal legend
Anne Boleyn was imprisoned and beheaded there
The central White Tower dates from 1078

westminster-abbaye.name: Westminster Abbey
descriptions: Almost every British monarch has been crowned there
Isaac Newton, Charles Darwin and Winston Churchill rest there
It has hosted royal funerals since medieval times
The current building dates from the 13th century under Henry III
Its towers were finished by Christopher Wren in 1745

windsor-castle.name: Windsor Castle
descriptions: It's the oldest continuously inhabited castle in the world
Saint George's Chapel is the royal burial place
It covers 13 hectares of grounds
Queen Victoria and Prince Albert are buried there
William and Harry grew up in its private apartments

edinburgh-castle.name: Edinburgh Castle
descriptions: It's built on an extinct volcano
It holds the Stone of Destiny, used for Scottish coronations
The One O'Clock Gun has been fired there daily since 1861
It was besieged more than 25 times in its history

oxford-bodleian.name: Bodleian Library
descriptions: It receives a legal copy of every book published in England
It holds more than 13 million books in its collections
The Duke Humfrey's Library dates from 1488
It served as Hogwarts library in the Harry Potter films
It owns a copy of the Magna Carta

st-pauls-cathedral.name: St Paul's Cathedral
descriptions: It was built after the Great Fire of London in 1666
Its Whispering Gallery carries sounds across 30 meters
Christopher Wren is buried in the crypt
It has shaped the City of London skyline for 300 years
Charles and Diana's wedding was held there in 1981

sagrada-familia.name: Sagrada Família
descriptions: Construction began in 1882 and is still ongoing
Antoni Gaudí worked on it for the last 43 years of his life
It's funded entirely by visitor entry fees
Gaudí is buried in its crypt
The Nativity facade and the Passion facade face opposite directions

alhambra.name: Alhambra
descriptions: Its name means 'the red one' in Arabic
The Generalife gardens sit right next to it
Its plaster stalactite carvings are called muqarnas
Nasrid sultans lived there until 1492

palais-royal-madrid.name: Royal Palace of Madrid
descriptions: It's the largest royal palace in Western Europe
It has 3,418 rooms over an area of 135,000 m²
The royal family has not lived there since 1931
Its Throne Room is still used for official ceremonies
Its Stradivarius violin collection is unique in the world

cathedrale-seville.name: Seville Cathedral
descriptions: It's the largest Gothic cathedral in the world
Christopher Columbus is buried there
It was built on the site of a large mosque
Its Giralda tower is the old minaret of the mosque
It has 80 side chapels

parc-guell.name: Park Güell
descriptions: Gaudí designed this park for a garden city that was never finished
Its trencadís mosaics recycle broken ceramics
The famous mosaic dragon has become a symbol of Barcelona
Gaudí lived there for the last 20 years of his life
The large wavy terrace can hold thousands of people

alcazar-seville.name: Alcázar of Seville
descriptions: It's the oldest royal palace still in use in Europe

Its construction began under the Umayyad caliphs

plaza-espana-seville.name: Plaza de España
descriptions: It was built for the 1929 Ibero-American Exposition

Alcoves represent each Spanish province

burgos-cathedrale.name: Burgos Cathedral

The Constable's Chapel is a masterpiece of Plateresque style
El Cid is buried there with his wife Jimena

acropole-athenes.name: Acropolis of Athens
descriptions: It towers over Athens from a rocky plateau 156 meters high
Pericles ordered its rebuilding in the 5th century BCE
The original statues are kept in the Acropolis Museum

parthenon.name: Parthenon
descriptions: It was dedicated to Athena Parthenos, protector of Athens
Its columns are slightly curved to appear straight
Lord Elgin took its friezes to London in the 19th century
The Panathenaic frieze was 160 meters long

temple-zeus-olympia.name: Temple of Zeus at Olympia
descriptions: It housed a giant ivory and gold statue of Zeus, one of the Seven Wonders
The statue was 13 meters tall
Earthquakes reduced the temple to fallen columns

palais-cnossos.name: Palace of Knossos
descriptions: It's the largest archaeological site in Crete

Arthur Evans excavated and restored it in the early 20th century
The palace had around 1,300 rooms

meteores.name: Meteora
descriptions: Monasteries are built atop rocky peaks 600 meters high
The name means 'suspended in the air' in Greek

The first monks reached them by nets and ladders

epidaure.name: Theatre of Epidaurus
descriptions: Its acoustics carry a voice to the back row
It can seat 14,000 spectators
It's still used for theater performances every summer
It was part of the sanctuary of Asclepius, god of medicine

chateau-neuschwanstein.name: Neuschwanstein Castle
descriptions: Ludwig II of Bavaria had it built as a romantic retreat

Its construction cost hundreds of millions of euros in today's money
Ludwig II only lived there 172 days before his mysterious death

porte-de-brandebourg.name: Brandenburg Gate
descriptions: It was built as a gate of peace

cathedrale-cologne.name: Cologne Cathedral

chateau-heidelberg.name: Heidelberg Castle
descriptions: It's one of the most iconic Renaissance ruins in Germany

memorial-holocaust-berlin.name: Memorial to the Murdered Jews of Europe
descriptions: It contains 2,711 concrete slabs of varying heights

palais-sans-souci.name: Sanssouci Palace
descriptions: Frederick the Great drew up the plans himself

Voltaire stayed there for three years

pont-regensburg.name: Stone Bridge of Regensburg
descriptions: It's the oldest stone bridge still standing in Germany

It's 336 meters long with 16 arches
It was the only stone bridge over the Danube for centuries

stephansdom-vienne.name: St. Stephen's Cathedral

schonbrunn.name: Schönbrunn Palace

Young Mozart gave his first concert there in 1762

belvedere-vienne.name: Belvedere Palace

hofburg-vienne.name: Hofburg Palace

tour-belem.name: Belém Tower

mosteiro-jeronimos.name: Jerónimos Monastery

palais-pena.name: Pena Palace

cathedrale-porto.name: Porto Cathedral

rijksmuseum-amsterdam.name: Rijksmuseum

Its neo-Gothic and Renaissance facade is decorated with sculptures

moulin-kinderdijk.name: Kinderdijk Windmills

palais-royal-amsterdam.name: Royal Palace of Amsterdam
descriptions: It was originally a town hall, one of the largest of the 17th century

grand-place-bruxelles.name: Grand Place

beffroi-bruges.name: Belfry of Bruges

cathedrale-anvers.name: Cathedral of Our Lady of Antwerp
descriptions: It's the largest Gothic cathedral in Belgium

atomium.name: Atomium
descriptions: It represents an iron molecule magnified 165 billion times

chateau-chillon.name: Chillon Castle

cathedrale-berne.name: Bern Minster

chateau-prague.name: Prague Castle

pont-charles-prague.name: Charles Bridge

Its foundation stone was laid at a time chosen by astrologers

cathedrale-saint-guy.name: St. Vitus Cathedral

horloge-astronomique-prague.name: Prague Astronomical Clock

parlement-budapest.name: Hungarian Parliament Building

bastion-pecheurs-budapest.name: Fisherman's Bastion

matyas-temple-budapest.name: Matthias Church

chateau-wawel.name: Wawel Castle

vieille-ville-varsovie.name: Old Town of Warsaw

chateau-malbork.name: Malbork Castle

saint-basile-moscou.name: Saint Basil's Cathedral

kremlin-moscou.name: Moscow Kremlin

ermitage-saint-petersbourg.name: Hermitage Museum

peterhof.name: Peterhof Palace

cathedrale-saint-isaac.name: Saint Isaac's Cathedral

cathedrale-nidaros.name: Nidaros Cathedral

palais-drottningholm.name: Drottningholm Palace

cathedrale-lund.name: Lund Cathedral

chapelle-temppeliaukio.name: Temppeliaukio Church
descriptions: It is carved entirely out of natural rock

Concerts are held there for its acoustics

roskilde-cathedrale.name: Roskilde Cathedral
descriptions: It has been the royal burial site of Denmark since the 10th century

palais-liechtenstein.name: Vaduz Castle
descriptions: It is the official residence of the princely family of Liechtenstein

palais-diocletien.name: Diocletian's Palace
descriptions: It is one of the best-preserved Roman palaces in the world
Emperor Diocletian retired here in 305

murs-dubrovnik.name: Walls of Dubrovnik
descriptions: The walls are 1,940 meters long and 25 meters high

George R.R. Martin chose Dubrovnik to film King's Landing
The walk along the top offers a panorama of the Adriatic

cathedrale-sibenik.name: Šibenik Cathedral
descriptions: It is one of the first large cathedrals built entirely of cut stone
Its 74 sculpted heads depict citizens of the time
Its cylindrical vault of stone slabs is unique in the world
It was built without mortar, with stones fitting together perfectly
Giorgio da Sebenico and Antonio Rizzo also worked on it

chateau-bratislava.name: Bratislava Castle
descriptions: It overlooks the Danube and the old town of Bratislava
Its four towers earned it the nickname 'upside-down turtle'
It was largely destroyed by fire in 1811 and later restored
It now houses the Slovak National Museum
It has belonged to Hungary, Austria, and Czechoslovakia

chateau-bled.name: Bled Castle
descriptions: It is the oldest castle in Slovenia
It overlooks the famous Lake Bled from 130 meters above
It houses a museum, a forge, and a medieval printing shop
Its terraces offer a view of the Julian Alps
The first written mention dates back to 1011

vieux-pont-mostar.name: Stari Most
descriptions: Its single 29-meter arch is a medieval engineering feat
It was destroyed in 1993 during the Bosnian War
Its identical reconstruction took 11 years
Local divers have been jumping from it for 600 years in competitions
It symbolizes the reconciliation between the communities of Mostar

kotor-vieux.name: Old Town of Kotor
descriptions: The Venetian walls climb up to 1,300 meters above sea level
The town is surrounded by the Bay of Kotor, the southernmost fjord in Europe
Its stray cats have become the tourist symbol of the city
The medieval old town is one of the best preserved in the Balkans
It was devastated by an earthquake in 1979 and later restored

cathedrale-sofia.name: Alexander Nevsky Cathedral
descriptions: It is one of the largest Orthodox cathedrals in the world
It is dedicated to the patron saint of Russia, who helped liberate Bulgaria
Its construction was partly funded by Russian donations
It can hold 5,000 worshippers under its 45-meter dome
It houses valuable murals and stained glass works

monastere-rila.name: Rila Monastery
descriptions: It is the largest and most famous monastery in Bulgaria
It was founded by Saint John of Rila, a Bulgarian hermit of the 10th century
It protected Bulgarian manuscripts and identity during Ottoman rule
Its vivid frescoes cover the porch arcades
It was entirely rebuilt after a fire in the 19th century

delphi.name: Sanctuary of Delphi
descriptions: The Greeks considered it the navel of the world
The Oracle of Delphi answered questions from kings and city-states
The Temple of Apollo bore the motto 'Know thyself'
Pan-Hellenic games were held here every four years
The site stretches over 570 meters in elevation on the slopes of Mount Parnassus

thessalonique-arche.name: Arch of Galerius
descriptions: It was built to celebrate the victory over the Persians and Armenians
It is the only Roman triumphal arch preserved in Greece
Its frieze depicts the military campaigns of Emperor Galerius
It was part of a larger imperial palace complex
It was originally covered with colored marble panels

newgrange.name: Newgrange
descriptions: It is older than Stonehenge and the Egyptian pyramids
The inner passage is lit up at sunrise on the winter solstice
Its construction required 200,000 tons of earth and rock
It is considered the best-preserved megalithic site in Europe
Access during the solstices was limited by a lottery

rock-of-cashel.name: Rock of Cashel
descriptions: According to legend, Saint Patrick baptized an Irish king here in the 5th century
It overlooks the Tipperary plain from a rocky outcrop
Cormac's Chapel from the 12th century is the best-known building on the site
It houses one of the most beautiful 9th-century Celtic crosses
The site was abandoned as a bishop's seat in 1749

cliffs-of-moher-tower.name: O'Brien's Tower
descriptions: It was built by John O'Brien to welcome visitors
The Cliffs of Moher rise up to 214 meters above the Atlantic
They welcome more than a million visitors each year
Dozens of seabird species nest on them
They were used as a filming location in Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince

chateau-bran.name: Bran Castle
descriptions: It is associated with Dracula, but Vlad the Impaler never stayed there
It served as a customs post between Transylvania and Wallachia
It was given to Queen Marie of Romania in 1920
Its secret passages and hidden staircases fascinate visitors
It is the most visited castle in Romania

parlement-bucarest.name: Palace of the Parliament
descriptions: It is the second-largest administrative building in the world after the Pentagon
Its construction ordered by Ceausescu destroyed an entire historic neighborhood
It has 1,100 rooms spread over 12 floors
It weighs 4 billion kilograms of concrete and contains 1 million m3 of marble
Construction involved up to 700 architects and 20,000 workers

monastere-voronet.name: Voroneț Monastery
descriptions: Its Voronet blue is a legendary color whose secret has been lost
The Last Judgment on its outer wall is exceptionally rich in detail
It was built in only three months according to tradition
Its outdoor frescoes have withstood the weather for over 500 years
It is nicknamed 'the Sistine Chapel of the East'

temples-tarxien.name: Tarxien Temples
descriptions: They form the largest megalithic complex in Malta
They predate the Egyptian pyramids by several centuries
Bones of more than 7,000 people have been found here
A fragmented statue of a mother goddess is one of the site's greatest mysteries
They were used as a burial and ceremonial site

fort-saint-ange.name: Fort Saint Angelo
descriptions: It defended the Grand Harbour of Malta for centuries
The Knights of Saint John made it their main stronghold
It resisted the Great Siege by the Ottomans in 1565
It is shared between the Order of Malta and the Maltese Armed Forces
Its origins date back to Phoenician antiquity

hallgrimskirkja.name: Hallgrímskirkja
descriptions: It is the largest church in Iceland
Its shape recalls the basalt columns found in Icelandic geology
Its 74.5-meter tower is visible from all over Reykjavik
Its construction took 41 years, from 1945 to 1986
It houses a concert organ with 5,275 pipes

saint-sava-belgrade.name: Cathedral of Saint Sava
descriptions: It is one of the largest Orthodox churches in the world
Its construction is still unfinished, having begun in 1935
It is dedicated to the founder of the Serbian Orthodox Church
Its central dome is 65 meters in diameter
Its interior mosaics still require around 400 years of work to complete

ohrid-sainte-sophie.name: Church of Saint Sophia, Ohrid
descriptions: It is one of the oldest churches in Southeastern Europe
It was turned into a mosque during 500 years of Ottoman rule
Its 11th-century frescoes are among the most precious in the Byzantine world
Lake Ohrid is one of the oldest lakes in the world
It is the cultural symbol of the UNESCO-listed town

aqueduct-segovia.name: Aqueduct of Segovia
descriptions: It has 166 arches stretching over 728 meters in length
It carried water for nearly 1,900 years
It is built without mortar, using only fitted granite blocks
It rises 28 meters at its highest point
It appears on the coat of arms of the city of Segovia

mezquita-cordoue.name: Mosque-Cathedral of Córdoba
descriptions: Its 856 jasper and marble columns form a forest of stone
At its peak, it was the second-largest mosque in the world
A cathedral was built in its center in the 16th century
Emir Abd al-Rahman I began its construction in 784
Its red and white striped arches became the symbol of Al-Andalus

casa-batllo.name: Casa Batlló
descriptions: Gaudi designed its facade to look like a scaly dragon
Its balcony shaped like carnival masks is unmistakable
The entire interior follows the organic shapes of the deep sea
It stands on Passeig de Gracia, the most elegant street in Barcelona
It was entirely remodeled by Gaudi between 1904 and 1906

gaudi-casa-mila.name: Casa Milà (La Pedrera)
descriptions: It is nicknamed La Pedrera ('the stone quarry')
Its wavy facade contains no right angles
Its chimneys shaped like masked warriors are iconic
Gaudi refused to decorate the facade with crucifixes for the anticlerical owner
Its rooftop terrace is open to visitors

palau-musica-catalana.name: Palau de la Música Catalana
descriptions: It is the only modernist concert hall listed by UNESCO
Its stained-glass dome lets natural light pour onto the stage
Its entire steel structure is wrapped in translucent bricks
It opened in 1908 with a concert by Pau Casals
It is the home of the Orfeo Catala choir

alcazar-tolede.name: Alcázar of Toledo
descriptions: It was turned into a military academy in the 19th century
It was severely damaged during the 1936 siege in the Spanish Civil War
Its postwar reconstruction made it a symbol of Franco's regime
It overlooks Toledo from a rocky hill above the Tagus River
It now houses a museum of the Spanish army

chateau-chambord.name: Château de Chambord
descriptions: Its double-helix staircase allegedly lets two people pass without seeing each other
It has 426 rooms, 77 staircases, and 282 fireplaces
Leonardo da Vinci is said to have influenced its architecture
King Francis I lived there for only 42 days in total
It is the largest chateau in the Loire Valley

amphitheatre-nimes.name: Arena of Nîmes
descriptions: It is the best-preserved Roman amphitheater in the world
It can still host 16,000 spectators for concerts
It has hosted bullfights since the Middle Ages
Its original Roman stands are still partly usable
It was built around the same time as the Colosseum in Rome

theatre-orange.name: Roman Theatre of Orange
descriptions: Its 103-meter-long stage wall is the only complete one left in the Roman world
King Louis XIV called it 'the finest wall in my kingdom'
It can host up to 9,000 spectators
Choirs and operas are still performed here every summer
The statue of Augustus at the center of the stage is the original

sainte-chapelle.name: Sainte-Chapelle
descriptions: Its stained-glass windows cover 600 m2 and are the oldest in Paris
It was built to house the Crown of Thorns of Christ
Its upper chapel is supported entirely by flying buttresses
It looks as though it is made almost entirely of glass
The relics it housed cost more to purchase than the building itself

chartres-cathedrale.name: Chartres Cathedral
descriptions: Its 167 medieval stained-glass windows are the most complete in the world
It has two mismatched spires, symbols of two different eras
Its floor labyrinth was laid out in the 12th century for pilgrims
Its Black Madonna has been an object of pilgrimage since the Middle Ages
It still inspires architects from around the world

chateau-amboise.name: Château d'Amboise
descriptions: Leonardo da Vinci spent the last three years of his life here
King Charles VIII died here in 1498 after hitting his head on a door lintel
Its Saint Hubert chapel is said to hold the remains of Leonardo da Vinci
Its cavalier tower allowed horsemen to ride straight up on horseback
It overlooks the Loire River and the Amboise valley

invalides-paris.name: Les Invalides
descriptions: Napoleon Bonaparte rests there in six nested coffins
It was founded by Louis XIV to house disabled soldiers
Its golden dome is one of the icons of the Paris skyline
Veterans still live there: around 80 residents today
The Army Museum holds 500,000 pieces of military history

catacombes-paris.name: Catacombs of Paris
descriptions: They hold the bones of more than 6 million Parisians
They were originally dug out as limestone quarries
The bones were moved here to ease overcrowded cemeteries in 1786
Their network of tunnels stretches over 300 km beneath Paris
Urban explorers called 'cataphiles' illegally visit the unopened sections

fontaine-de-vaucluse.name: Fontaine-de-Vaucluse
descriptions: It is the most powerful spring in France
It rises from a vertical chasm more than 300 meters deep
The poet Petrarch lived here and was inspired to write his sonnets to Laura
Its flow can reach 200 m3 per second during flood periods
The name Vaucluse comes from the Latin Vallis Clausa, 'closed valley'

abbaye-cluny.name: Cluny Abbey
descriptions: For two centuries it was the largest church in the Christian world
Its abbot oversaw more than 1,000 monasteries across Europe
It was largely demolished after the French Revolution
Today only the bell tower and one bay of the transept remain
It was at the heart of the monastic revival of the 11th century

tour-saint-jacques.name: Tour Saint-Jacques
descriptions: It is all that remains of a church destroyed during the French Revolution
It served as a starting point of the Way of Saint James to Santiago de Compostela
Blaise Pascal carried out atmospheric pressure experiments here
It stands 52 meters tall and is in the Flamboyant Gothic style
It was long used as a lead quarry

chateau-chenonceau.name: Château de Chenonceau
descriptions: Its arched gallery spans the river Cher
It was offered by King Henry II to Diane de Poitiers
Catherine de Medici expanded it with a two-story gallery
During World War I, the gallery was used as a hospital
It is the most visited privately owned chateau in France

teatro-olimpico-vicenza.name: Teatro Olimpico
descriptions: It is the oldest indoor theater in the world still in use
Andrea Palladio died before its opening in 1585
Its trompe-l'oeil stage creates the illusion of deep streets
The painted perspectives in its wings have never been changed
Its semicircular cavea can seat 1,000 spectators

castel-del-monte.name: Castel del Monte
descriptions: Its octagonal shape is unique in medieval architecture
Each corner tower is also octagonal
The octagon symbolizes the link between the divine circle and the earthly square
Frederick II was the only ruler ever to live there
Its exact purpose, whether hunting lodge or observatory, remains a mystery

palerme-cathedrale.name: Palermo Cathedral
descriptions: It reflects 800 years of Norman, Arab, Gothic, and Baroque influences
The tombs of the Norman and Swabian emperors rest here
It features a remarkable solar meridian set into the floor
Its facade combines pointed arches with domes
The kings of Sicily were crowned here from the 12th century onwards

uffizi-florence.name: Uffizi Gallery
descriptions: It houses The Birth of Venus and The Primavera by Botticelli
It was built to host the offices (uffizi) of the Florentine government
The Medici family turned it into an art gallery in the 16th and 17th centuries
It holds one of the largest collections of Renaissance paintings
A neo-fascist bombing killed 5 people inside it in 1993

capella-sistine.name: Sistine Chapel
descriptions: Michelangelo painted the ceiling lying on a scaffold for 4 years
The Creation of Adam is its most famous fresco
Papal conclaves have been held here since 1492
White smoke from its chimney announces the election of a pope
The Last Judgment on the altar wall was painted 25 years later

arc-titus-rome.name: Arch of Titus
descriptions: It is the oldest Roman triumphal arch in the Forum
It commemorates the capture of Jerusalem and the destruction of the Temple in 70
Its depiction of the Menorah is the only known ancient image of it
It served as a model for every modern triumphal arch in Europe
Napoleon used it as inspiration for the Arc de Triomphe in Paris

valle-dei-templi.name: Valley of the Temples
descriptions: It is the best-preserved Greek archaeological site outside of Greece
The Temple of Concordia is one of the finest Doric temples in the world
The Valley stretches over 1,300 hectares
It was the city of Akragas, one of the wealthiest in the Greek world
The poet Pindar described it as 'the most beautiful of mortal cities'

cathedrale-florence.name: Florence Baptistery
descriptions: Its ceiling of golden mosaics depicts the Last Judgment
It is one of the oldest Christian baptisteries in the world
Dante Alighieri was baptized here in 1265
Its bronze doors by Ghiberti were called by Michelangelo 'the Gates of Paradise'
Its construction over several centuries gave it three different styles

chateau-kruje.name: Krujë Castle
descriptions: It was the stronghold of George Castriot Skanderbeg against the Ottomans
Skanderbeg held out here for 25 years against the armies of Mehmed II
It is a symbol of Albanian national identity
Its medieval Ottoman bazaar is still active today
The Skanderbeg national museum is built within its walls

corinthe-antique.name: Acrocorinth
descriptions: It is one of the most imposing natural citadels in Greece
Its ramparts stretch for more than 2 km around the site
It was once the largest fortress in the Byzantine world
Its highest point, at 575 meters, overlooks the Gulf of Corinth
It changed hands between Greeks, Byzantines, Crusaders, Ottomans, and Venetians

forteresse-suomenlinna.name: Suomenlinna Fortress
descriptions: It is built across 6 islands connected by bridges
It was built to resist Russian naval attacks
Thousands of soldiers worked on its construction
It is the largest sea fortress in Scandinavia
About a thousand people still live there permanently

cathedrale-helsinki.name: Helsinki Cathedral
descriptions: Its green dome is the symbol of the Helsinki skyline
It stands at the top of Senate Square
It was designed in the neoclassical style of the Russian Empire
Its rooftop statues of the apostles are among the largest in the world
It was dedicated to Saint Nicholas, the patron saint of sailors

maison-tetes-noires-riga.name: House of the Blackheads
descriptions: It was built for the guild of unmarried merchants
The 'Black Heads' refer to Saint Maurice, their African patron saint
It was completely destroyed in 1941 and faithfully rebuilt in 1999
Its Flemish Renaissance facade is adorned with bas-reliefs and coats of arms
It is the most iconic landmark in Riga's old town

cathedrale-tallinn.name: Alexander Nevsky Cathedral, Tallinn
descriptions: It is the largest Orthodox cathedral in the Baltic states
It was built in tribute to Russian sailors who drowned at sea
Estonians long viewed this monument as an imposed Russian symbol
Its five onion domes tower over the medieval old town
It was built while Tallinn was under Russian Empire rule

chateau-trakai.name: Trakai Island Castle
descriptions: It is built on an island in the middle of a lake
It was the main residence of Grand Duke Vytautas of Lithuania
It is one of the few Gothic island castles in Northern Europe
It was completely restored between 1955 and 1961
The local Karaim community has lived here since the 14th century

tour-de-la-vierge-bakou.name: Maiden Tower
descriptions: It is the oldest and most mysterious tower in the old city of Baku
Its exact purpose, observatory, lighthouse, or temple, is still debated
It stands 29 meters tall and 16 meters in diameter
An Arabic inscription mentions a 12th-century stonemason
It gave its nickname to the UNESCO-listed old town

cathedrale-sainte-sophie-kiev.name: Saint Sophia Cathedral, Kyiv
descriptions: It is one of the finest examples of Byzantine architecture in Europe
Its name and layout are directly inspired by Hagia Sophia in Constantinople
It contains nearly intact 11th-century mosaics and frescoes
Grand Duke Yaroslav the Wise had it built after a victory
It survived the Mongol destruction of 1240 thanks to its sacred status

monastere-petchersk.name: Kyiv Pechersk Lavra
descriptions: Its underground catacombs hold the remains of mummified monks
It is one of the oldest Slavic Orthodox monasteries
Its name means 'monastery of the caves' in Ukrainian
Orthodox pilgrims come here from all over Eastern Europe
It was founded by hermits who carved cells into the cliffside

rocher-de-gibraltar.name: Rock of Gibraltar
descriptions: It was one of the two Pillars of Hercules in ancient times
Its network of military tunnels is 54 km long
A colony of Barbary macaques has lived on its cliffs for centuries
Legend says that if the monkeys disappear, Gibraltar will fall
It is one of the most strategic points in the Mediterranean

eglise-sant-esteve.name: Sant Esteve Church
descriptions: It is the main parish church of Andorra la Vella
It dates back to the 11th century but has been remodeled several times
Its Romanesque bell is one of the oldest in the country
It is dedicated to Saint Stephen, the first Christian martyr
It stands in the heart of Andorra's historic old quarter

monastere-geghard.name: Geghard Monastery
descriptions: Part of the monastery is carved entirely out of solid rock
It once held a spear said to have pierced the side of Christ
Its Armenian name Geghard means 'the spear'
Its sacred polyphonic music is listed as UNESCO heritage
It was founded in the 4th century on a sacred spring

eglise-sameba-tbilisi.name: Holy Trinity Cathedral of Tbilisi
descriptions: It is the largest cathedral in the Caucasus
Its construction marks the 1,500th anniversary of the Georgian Church's autocephaly
Its dome reaches 87 meters in height
It is surrounded by gardens on Elia hill
Worshippers simply call it Sameba, 'the Trinity'

skopje-forteresse.name: Skopje Fortress
descriptions: It overlooks central Skopje from a rocky hilltop
It was one of the main Byzantine fortresses of the 11th century
An earthquake in 1963 partially damaged it
Its walls offer a panorama of the Vardar valley
Excavations have revealed remains dating back to the Neolithic era

butrint.name: Butrint
descriptions: It was inhabited in turn by the Greeks, Romans, Byzantines, and Venetians
The harbor city is now buried in a lush tropical forest
Its 3rd-century BC Greek theater is remarkably well preserved
Virgil mentions Butrint in the Aeneid as 'Little Troy'
The site is surrounded by a lake and a channel

vieux-luxembourg.name: Old Town of Luxembourg
descriptions: Its underground fortifications, the Bock Casemates, stretch over 23 km
The city was nicknamed 'the Gibraltar of the North' for its defenses
It was dismantled by order of European powers in 1867
It was one of the best-defended cities in Europe in its time
Count Siegfried founded it by trading away monastic land

taj-mahal.name: Taj Mahal
descriptions: A mausoleum built by Emperor Shah Jahan for his wife Mumtaz Mahal
Its white marble facade changes color throughout the day
Its construction involved about 20,000 workers over 21 years
It is perfectly symmetrical, except for the emperor's added tomb
It is one of the new seven wonders of the world

cite-interdite.name: Forbidden City
descriptions: Largest imperial palace in the world with 980 buildings
It was the residence of 24 emperors of the Ming and Qing dynasties
Its red walls symbolize luck and prosperity in China
Its name comes from the ban on entering without imperial permission
Listed as a UNESCO World Heritage Site since 1987

grande-muraille-de-chine.name: Great Wall of China
descriptions: Its total length is about 21,196 kilometers
It is not visible to the naked eye from the Moon, contrary to legend
Millions of workers, soldiers, and prisoners took part in its construction
Some sections date back to the 7th century BC
It is one of the new seven wonders of the world

qutb-minar.name: Qutb Minar
descriptions: Tallest brick minaret in the world at 72.5 meters
Its construction began in 1193 after the Muslim conquest of Delhi
The minaret has five levels, each in a distinct architectural style
Quranic inscriptions decorate every floor of the tower
Listed as a UNESCO World Heritage Site since 1993

hawa-mahal.name: Hawa Mahal
descriptions: Its name means Palace of the Winds in Hindi
Its facade has 953 small windows decorated with latticework screens
It was built to allow women of the court to watch the street
Its main pink sandstone facade has five floors
It was built by Maharaja Sawai Pratap Singh in 1799

fort-rouge.name: Red Fort
descriptions: Residence of the Mughal emperors of India for two centuries
Its red sandstone walls give the fort its name
This is where India proclaimed its independence on August 15, 1947
The fort covers an area of 254 acres
Listed as a UNESCO World Heritage Site since 2007

temple-or-amritsar.name: Golden Temple
descriptions: The holiest site in Sikhism, visited by 100,000 people every day
Its dome is covered with 750 kilograms of real gold
It is surrounded by a sacred lake called Amrit Sarovar (pool of nectar)
The temple offers a free meal to thousands of pilgrims every day
Its entrance is open to anyone, regardless of religion

khajuraho.name: Khajuraho Temples
descriptions: Famous for its erotic sculptures on the outer walls of the temples
Of 85 temples originally built, only 25 have survived to this day
The sculptures depict every aspect of human life
These temples were built by the Chandela dynasty between the 10th and 12th centuries
Listed as a UNESCO World Heritage Site since 1986

stupa-sanchi.name: Great Stupa of Sanchi
descriptions: Oldest Buddhist building still standing in India
Emperor Ashoka had it built in the 3rd century BC
It is said to hold relics of the Buddha
Its carved gateways depict the life of the Buddha in detail
Listed as a UNESCO World Heritage Site since 1989

hampi.name: Hampi Ruins
descriptions: Former capital of the powerful Vijayanagara Empire
It was one of the largest cities in the world in the 16th century
The site has more than 1,600 monuments spread over 41 km2
The city was sacked and destroyed in 1565 after the defeat at Talikota
Listed as a UNESCO World Heritage Site since 1986

mysore-palace.name: Mysore Palace
descriptions: Third most-visited tourist site in India after the Taj Mahal and Tirupati
The current palace was rebuilt in 1912 after a fire
It is lit up by 97,000 light bulbs every Sunday and public holiday
It blends Indo-Saracenic, Hindu, Muslim, and Gothic styles
Residence of the maharajas of Mysore for nearly two centuries

temple-du-ciel.name: Temple of Heaven
descriptions: Emperors of China came here every year to pray for a good harvest
Built according to the principles of feng shui and Chinese cosmology
Its blue tile roof symbolizes the sky
The Hall of Prayer for Good Harvests stands without a single nail
Listed as a UNESCO World Heritage Site since 1998

armee-terracotta.name: Terracotta Army
descriptions: It was discovered by accident in 1974 by farmers digging a well
It includes more than 8,000 soldiers, 130 chariots, and 670 horses in terracotta
Every soldier's face is unique and individualized
These figures guarded the tomb of the first emperor Qin Shi Huang
Listed as a UNESCO World Heritage Site since 1987

bouddha-leshan.name: Leshan Giant Buddha
descriptions: The largest stone Buddha statue in the world at 71 meters tall
It took 90 years to carve, from 713 to 803 AD
The Buddha's ears are 7 meters long
Hidden drainage channels protect the statue from erosion
Listed as a UNESCO World Heritage Site since 1996

palais-d-ete.name: Summer Palace
descriptions: It spans more than 290 hectares, three quarters of which are covered by water
Empress Dowager Cixi diverted naval funds to rebuild it
Kunming Lake was dug entirely by hand by thousands of workers
The Long Corridor stretches 728 meters with 14,000 decorative paintings
Listed as a UNESCO World Heritage Site since 1998

tour-shanghai.name: Shanghai Tower
descriptions: Second-tallest tower in the world at 632 meters
Its twisted shape reduces wind forces on the structure by 24%
It has the fastest elevators in the world at 74 km/h
Its spiral design is inspired by Chinese nature traditions
It is LEED Gold certified for its energy efficiency

tour-perle-orient.name: Oriental Pearl Tower
descriptions: It was the tallest tower in Asia when it opened in 1994
Its two spheres recall pearls placed along the Huangpu River
It houses an aquarium, a hotel, and a Shanghai museum
Its 11 spheres represent 11 colorful orbs of different sizes
It remains one of the most recognizable symbols of Shanghai

potala-palace.name: Potala Palace
descriptions: Former residence of the Dalai Lama, at 3,700 meters altitude
The palace has 1,000 rooms, 10,000 shrines, and 200,000 statues
Its construction took over 50 years, from 1645 to 1694
Its interior walls are 5 meters thick at the base
Listed as a UNESCO World Heritage Site since 1994

pagode-wild-goose.name: Giant Wild Goose Pagoda
descriptions: It was built to house Buddhist sutras brought back from India
Monk Xuanzang oversaw its construction after his 17-year pilgrimage
The pagoda is 64 meters tall and has seven floors
Its name comes from a legend where monks found a wild goose fallen from the sky
Listed as a UNESCO World Heritage Site since 2014

mont-wudang.name: Wudang Mountains Temples
descriptions: Major Taoist site with temples built over 1,500 years
The site contains 72 temples and 36 monasteries across the mountain slopes
The golden hall at the summit is made entirely of gilded bronze
Legend says the immortal Xuanwu cultivated himself on this mountain
Listed as a UNESCO World Heritage Site since 1994

cite-pingyao.name: Ancient City of Pingyao
descriptions: One of the best-preserved Chinese cities from the feudal era
Its 17th-century walls stretch over 6.4 km
The city was a major financial center of China in the 19th century
China's first private bank was founded here in 1823
Listed as a UNESCO World Heritage Site since 1997

mont-fuji.name: Mount Fuji
descriptions: Tallest mountain in Japan at 3,776 meters
An active volcano whose last eruption was in 1707
National symbol of Japan, depicted in art for centuries
About 300,000 people climb Mount Fuji every year
Listed as a UNESCO World Heritage Site since 2013

torii-miyajima.name: Itsukushima Torii
descriptions: Its torii gate appears to float on the water at high tide
The Itsukushima shrine has existed since the 6th century
Historically, it was forbidden to be born or to die on the island
The current torii, made of camphor wood, dates back to 1875
Listed as a UNESCO World Heritage Site since 1996

temple-kinkakuji.name: Kinkaku-ji (Golden Pavilion)
descriptions: Its top two floors are entirely covered in gold leaf
It was burned down in 1950 by a Buddhist novice obsessed with its beauty
The current temple is a faithful reconstruction from 1955
It is surrounded by a Zen garden designed in the 14th century
It has been a UNESCO World Heritage Site since 1994

temple-sensoji.name: Sensō-ji Temple
descriptions: Tokyo's oldest temple, founded in 645 AD
It is dedicated to Kannon, the Buddhist goddess of mercy
Its Kaminarimon gate houses a giant lantern weighing 670 kg
More than 30 million visitors come here each year
It was rebuilt after being destroyed in the 1945 bombings

chateau-himeji.name: Himeji Castle
descriptions: Nicknamed the White Heron Castle for its immaculate color
It is the best-preserved medieval Japanese castle in the country
Its defenses include 83 buildings linked by maze-like corridors
No major changes have been made since the 17th century
It has been a UNESCO World Heritage Site since 1993

sanctuaire-fushimi-inari.name: Fushimi Inari Shrine
descriptions: Famous for its thousands of vermillion-orange torii gates lined up like a tunnel
It is dedicated to Inari, the Shinto deity of rice, foxes, and trade
The main path climbs to the top of Mount Inari at 233 meters
Thousands of stone foxes guard the entrance to the shrine
It is the most visited Shinto shrine in Japan

temple-ginkakuji.name: Ginkaku-ji (Silver Pavilion)
descriptions: Its name means Silver Pavilion, though it was never covered in silver
It was built as a retirement villa for the shogun Ashikaga Yoshimasa
Its dry Zen garden is famous for its sand cone symbolizing Mount Fuji
The temple is a perfect example of the Japanese wabi-sabi aesthetic
It has been a UNESCO World Heritage Site since 1994

tour-tokyo.name: Tokyo Tower
descriptions: Inspired by the Eiffel Tower, it stands 13 meters taller at 333 meters
It was built in just 18 months after World War II
Its orange and white color is required by civil aviation rules
It served as the main communications tower until the Tokyo Skytree was built
About 3 million visitors climb it each year

tokyo-skytree.name: Tokyo Skytree
descriptions: The second tallest man-made structure in the world at 634 meters
Opened in 2012, it has become the symbol of modern Tokyo
It houses two public observatories at 350 and 450 meters
Its height of 634 meters recalls Tokyo's old name, Musashi
It resists earthquakes thanks to a central shock-absorbing pillar

nara-daibutsu.name: Great Buddha of Nara
descriptions: The largest bronze Buddha in the world at 14.7 meters tall
It weighs around 500 tons of bronze
Its construction used almost all of the bronze available in Japan
The temple that houses it, Todai-ji, is the largest wooden building in the world
It has been a UNESCO World Heritage Site since 1998

chateau-osaka.name: Osaka Castle
descriptions: It was at the heart of Japan's unification by Toyotomi Hideyoshi
Its outer walls were built with stones weighing up to 130 tons
It was besieged, burned, and rebuilt several times throughout history
The current castle tower dates from a 1931 reconstruction
Hundreds of cherry trees bloom around the castle each spring

angkor-vat.name: Angkor Wat
descriptions: The largest religious complex in the world, covering 402 acres
Built in the 12th century for the Khmer king Suryavarman II
Originally dedicated to Vishnu, it became Buddhist in the 13th century
Its gallery of bas-reliefs is 800 meters long
The image of the temple appears on Cambodia's flag

bayon.name: Bayon Temple
descriptions: Famous for its 216 smiling faces carved in stone
State temple of the Khmer king Jayavarman VII, a devoted Buddhist
Its towers are believed by some to represent the Bodhisattva Avalokitesvara
The bas-reliefs depict naval battles and scenes from daily life
It has been a UNESCO World Heritage Site since 1992

ta-prohm.name: Ta Prohm
descriptions: Its giant trees grow over the ruins, creating a striking effect
Built in 1186 to house the monastery and university of King Jayavarman VII
It was used as a filming location for Lara Croft Tomb Raider in 2001
The site once hosted more than 12,000 people and 260 dancers
It has been a UNESCO World Heritage Site since 1992

wat-phra-kaew.name: Wat Phra Kaew
descriptions: The most important Buddhist temple in Thailand, located within the Grand Palace grounds
It houses the Emerald Buddha statue, only 66 cm tall
The King of Thailand changes the Buddha's clothing himself three times a year
Its roofs of green and orange ceramic tiles shine in the sun
No monks live in this temple, only royal guards

wat-arun.name: Wat Arun
descriptions: Its name means Temple of Dawn in Thai
Its central tower rises 86 meters above the Chao Phraya River
Its surface is inlaid with fragments of colorful porcelain
It was embellished under the reign of King Rama II in the 19th century
It is one of the most iconic monuments in Bangkok

bouddha-couche-wat-pho.name: Reclining Buddha of Wat Pho
descriptions: The statue is 46 meters long and 15 meters tall
The Buddha's feet are decorated with 108 sacred symbols in mother-of-pearl
Wat Pho is the oldest and largest temple in Bangkok
The temple also houses the oldest traditional Thai massage center
The statue represents Buddha entering Nirvana

ayutthaya.name: Ayutthaya Ruins
descriptions: Former capital of the Kingdom of Siam, founded in 1350
It was one of the largest cities in the world in the 17th century with 1 million inhabitants
The city was razed by the Burmese in 1767 after a 15-month siege
You can still find Buddha heads tangled in tree roots there
It has been a UNESCO World Heritage Site since 1991

phimai.name: Phimai Temple
descriptions: The largest Khmer temple in Thailand, an architectural ancestor of Angkor Wat
Built in the 11th and 12th centuries under Khmer Empire rule
It is reached via a naga bridge with mythological serpent heads
Its central prang is 28 meters tall, made of white sandstone
It was directly linked to Angkor by a royal road of 225 km

bai-dinh.name: Bai Dinh Pagoda
descriptions: The largest Buddhist complex in Southeast Asia, covering 700 hectares
It houses the largest bronze bell in Vietnam, weighing 36 tons
Its corridors hold 500 stone statues of arhats
Its Great Bell Tower is 45 meters tall
It draws millions of pilgrims during the Tet festival each year

hue-citadelle.name: Citadel of Huế
descriptions: Former imperial capital of the Nguyen dynasty of Vietnam
Its ramparts are 10 km in perimeter and 6 meters high
It was the site of intense fighting during the Battle of Hue in 1968
The Imperial City inside was inspired by Beijing's Forbidden City
It has been a UNESCO World Heritage Site since 1993

my-son.name: My Son Sanctuary
descriptions: Former religious center of the Cham Kingdom, active from the 4th to the 13th century
The site has more than 70 temples dedicated to the god Shiva
It was heavily damaged by American bombing during the Vietnam War
The temples are built from bricks bonded with a mysterious plant resin
It has been a UNESCO World Heritage Site since 1999

hoi-an.name: Hoi An Ancient Town
descriptions: A thriving trading port from the 15th to the 19th century, open to merchants from around the world
Its cobbled streets are filled with colorful lanterns every evening
The old town has preserved the architecture of Chinese, Japanese, and French merchants
The Japanese Covered Bridge was built here in the 17th century without a single nail
It has been a UNESCO World Heritage Site since 1999

borobudur.name: Borobudur
descriptions: The largest Buddhist monument in the world, with 2,672 bas-relief panels
Built in the 8th century, it was abandoned and buried under volcanic ash
It contains 504 Buddha statues and 72 openwork stupas
Its layout represents a three-dimensional mandala symbolizing the universe
It has been a UNESCO World Heritage Site since 1991

prambanan.name: Prambanan Temple
descriptions: The largest Hindu temple on Java, dedicated to the Trimurti (Brahma, Vishnu, Shiva)
The complex includes 240 temples built in the 9th century
Its central tower is 47 meters tall
It has been damaged by many earthquakes throughout its history
It has been a UNESCO World Heritage Site since 1991

shwedagon.name: Shwedagon Pagoda
descriptions: The most sacred Buddhist pagoda in Myanmar
Its golden spire rises 99 meters above the platform
The top of the pagoda is decorated with more than 5,000 diamonds and rubies
It is covered in gold leaf totaling 60 tons
Legend says it holds 8 sacred hairs of the Buddha

bagan.name: Bagan Temples
descriptions: A plain dotted with more than 2,000 temples and pagodas from the 9th to 13th century
At its peak, the region had more than 10,000 religious buildings
The temples were built by the kings of the first Burmese empire
Hot air balloon rides offer views of the temples at sunrise
It has been a UNESCO World Heritage Site since 2019

tour-kl.name: Kuala Lumpur Tower
descriptions: The seventh tallest telecommunications tower in the world
It is 421 meters tall and was opened in 1996
Its design is inspired by the bumbu, a traditional Malaysian cooking utensil
It houses a rotating panoramic restaurant at 335 meters
Its foundations reach 35 meters deep into the bedrock

marina-bay-sands.name: Marina Bay Sands
descriptions: Its boat-shaped roof rests on three 55-story towers
The rooftop infinity pool is the largest in the world at this height
The hotel houses a casino, a museum, and a huge shopping mall
Its construction cost 8 billion Singapore dollars
Architect Moshe Safdie drew inspiration from a deck of cards for its shape

merlion.name: Merlion
descriptions: Singapore's official symbol since 1964, half lion, half fish
The lion represents Singapore's old name, Singapura (lion city)
The fish symbolizes the city's origins as a fishing village
The main statue is 8.6 meters tall and weighs 70 tons
It spouts water toward Marina Bay

chocolate-hills.name: Chocolate Hills
descriptions: More than 1,200 cone-shaped hills covered in brown grass during the dry season
Their chocolate color in the dry season gives them their popular name
Their origin is still debated, between erosion and uplifted coral formations
They have become the provincial symbol of the island of Bohol
Filipino legend says they are the tears of a giant in love

gyeongbokgung.name: Gyeongbokgung Palace
descriptions: Main palace of the Joseon dynasty, founded in 1395
Its name means Palace of Shining Happiness
It was burned down by Japanese invaders in 1592 and rebuilt in 1867
It includes more than 500 buildings across 40 hectares
Guards in traditional Joseon costume perform the changing of the guard ceremony

bulguksa.name: Bulguksa Temple
descriptions: Temple founded in 528, a showcase of Silla Buddhist architecture
Its stone staircases represent the passage from the earthly world to paradise
It houses two pagodas classified as Korean national treasures
Destroyed during the Japanese invasion in 1593, it was restored in the 20th century
It has been a UNESCO World Heritage Site since 1995

suwon-hwaseong.name: Hwaseong Fortress
descriptions: Fortress built by King Jeongjo to honor his imprisoned father
It combines Chinese and Korean military construction techniques
Its walls stretch 5.7 km and include 48 defensive structures
It was built in only 2 years and 9 months, from 1794 to 1796
It has been a UNESCO World Heritage Site since 1997

haeinsa.name: Haeinsa Temple
descriptions: Temple housing the Tripitaka Koreana, the oldest collection of Buddhist texts
The 80,000 wooden blocks of the Tripitaka date from the 13th century
The ventilation system in the buildings that hold the blocks is remarkable
The temple is one of the Three Jewel Temples of Korean Buddhism
It has been a UNESCO World Heritage Site since 1995

changdeokgung.name: Changdeokgung Palace
descriptions: A favorite of Joseon dynasty kings for its natural beauty
Its Secret Garden spans 78 acres of woods and pavilions
It was the last palace to house the imperial family, until 1907
Its architecture follows the principle of blending harmoniously with nature
It has been a UNESCO World Heritage Site since 1997

boudhanath.name: Boudhanath Stupa
descriptions: One of the largest Buddhist stupas in the world, 36 meters tall
Its painted Buddha eyes gaze in all four cardinal directions
It is the spiritual center of the Tibetan community in exile in Nepal
Thousands of devotees walk around the stupa reciting mantras
It has been a UNESCO World Heritage Site since 1979

pashupatinath.name: Pashupatinath Temple
descriptions: The most sacred Hindu temple in Nepal, dedicated to the god Shiva
Access to the inside of the temple is forbidden to non-Hindus
Ritual cremations take place every day on the ghats of the Bagmati
Hundreds of sadhus (holy men) live there permanently
It has been a UNESCO World Heritage Site since 1979

swayambhunath.name: Swayambhunath Stupa
descriptions: Nicknamed Monkey Temple for the many primates that live there
Perched on a hill 77 meters above Kathmandu
One of the oldest religious sites in Nepal, around 2,500 years old
Its white stupa symbolizes the five elements of the Buddhist universe
It has been a UNESCO World Heritage Site since 1979

sigiriya.name: Sigiriya Rock
descriptions: Fortress built in the 5th century on a 200-meter granite rock
King Kashyapa I had 500 frescoes of heavenly women painted there
The summit is reached by stairs through the mouth of a giant lion
The complex includes gardens, pools, and gravity-fed fountains
It has been a UNESCO World Heritage Site since 1982

temple-dent-kandy.name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
descriptions: It holds the sacred tooth relic of the Buddha, which arrived in Sri Lanka in the 4th century
Only senior religious figures may approach the relic during ceremonies
The Esala Perahera festival gathers elephants decorated with gold here each year
The temple was rebuilt after being looted by the Portuguese in the 16th century
It has been a UNESCO World Heritage Site since 1988

mohenjo-daro.name: Mohenjo-daro
descriptions: One of the largest cities of the Indus Valley civilization, around 2500 BC
It had about 40,000 inhabitants, one of the densest ancient urban centers
The city had an advanced sewer and drainage system
Its name means Mound of the Dead in the Sindhi language
It has been a UNESCO World Heritage Site since 1980

badshahi-mosque.name: Badshahi Mosque
descriptions: One of the largest mosques in the world, holding up to 100,000 worshippers
Built by Mughal Emperor Aurangzeb between 1671 and 1673
Its four 53-meter minarets border a vast marble courtyard
It was used as an arsenal by the Sikhs in the 19th century
Its main gate is inspired by Persian architecture

lahore-fort.name: Lahore Fort
descriptions: Imperial citadel whose origins go back to the 10th century
Each Mughal emperor added his own buildings to the fort
The Diwan-e-Khas holds the emperors' white marble throne
Its 6-meter-high walls stretch for more than a kilometer
It has been a UNESCO World Heritage Site since 1981

sainte-sophie.name: Hagia Sophia
sainte-sophie.architect: Isidore of Miletus & Anthemius of Tralles
descriptions: Its 31-meter-wide dome was the largest in the world for a thousand years
Built in just 5 years by Emperor Justinian I
It has been a cathedral, a mosque, a museum, and again a mosque since 2020
Its architects Isidore and Anthemius used a revolutionary pendentive vaulting technique
It has been a UNESCO World Heritage Site since 1985

mosquee-bleue.name: Blue Mosque
descriptions: Its nickname comes from the 21,043 blue Iznik tiles that decorate its interior
It is the only mosque in Istanbul with six minarets
Built between 1609 and 1616 by Sedefkar Mehmed Agha for Sultan Ahmed I
Its outer courtyard is as large as the inside of the mosque
It faces Hagia Sophia and borrows some of its architectural features

ephese.name: Ruins of Ephesus
descriptions: Ancient Greek and Roman city that held the Temple of Artemis, one of the Seven Wonders
It was the second most populous city of the Roman Empire after Rome
The Library of Celsus could hold 12,000 parchment scrolls
Saint Paul is said to have stayed there and written his epistles
It has been a UNESCO World Heritage Site since 2015

cappadoce.name: Cappadocia Fairy Chimneys
descriptions: A landscape of volcanic rocks shaped by erosion over millions of years
Christians dug underground cities here to escape persecution
Thousands of hot air balloons rise here every morning at sunrise
The cave dwellings were lived in until the 20th century
It has been a UNESCO World Heritage Site since 1985

topkapi.name: Topkapi Palace
descriptions: The main Ottoman palace, seat of the empire's government for 400 years
It holds the cloak of the Prophet Muhammad and other Islamic relics
Its harem sometimes held more than 1,000 women
It covers 700,000 m² with 400 rooms and 4 inner courtyards
It has been a UNESCO World Heritage Site since 1985

mosquee-imam-isfahan.name: Shah Mosque of Isfahan
descriptions: A masterpiece of Islamic architecture from the Safavid era
Its main portal is 27 meters tall, decorated with blue mosaics
Its 52-meter dome produces a 7-second echo at its center
Its construction took 18 years during the reign of Shah Abbas I
It has been a UNESCO World Heritage Site since 1979

place-naqsh-e-jahan.name: Naqsh-e Jahan Square
descriptions: The second largest public square in the world, after Tiananmen Square
It is 512 meters long and 163 meters wide
It is one of the largest Islamic architectural complexes in the world
It was used as a polo field by Safavid rulers
It has been a UNESCO World Heritage Site since 1979

tchogha-zanbil.name: Tchogha Zanbil
descriptions: The best-preserved Elamite ziggurat in the world, built around 1250 BC
It was dedicated to Inshushinak, the supreme Elamite god
Only three of the original five levels have survived to this day
It was rediscovered through aerial photos in 1935
It has been a UNESCO World Heritage Site since 1979

pasargades.name: Pasargadae
descriptions: First capital of the Achaemenid Persian Empire, founded by Cyrus the Great
It holds the tomb of Cyrus II, regarded as the first defender of human rights
The gardens of Pasargadae are the oldest known Persian gardens
Cyrus's tomb was long mistaken for the tomb of Solomon's mother
It has been a UNESCO World Heritage Site since 2004

petra.name: Petra
descriptions: Carved into the pink rock by the Nabateans more than 2,000 years ago
It is reached through a 1.5 km canyon called the Siq
Its most famous monument, the Treasury, was used as a set for Indiana Jones
The city has up to 800 monuments carved into the cliffs
Listed among the New Seven Wonders of the World

dome-rocher.name: Dome of the Rock
descriptions: The oldest Islamic shrine still standing, built in 691
Its golden dome covers the rock from which the Prophet Muhammad is said to have ascended
The dome has been covered with 5,000 gold plates since its restoration in 1994
It stands on the Temple Mount, a sacred site for the three Abrahamic religions
Its glass and mother-of-pearl mosaic is one of the finest examples of Islamic decoration

mur-lamentation.name: Western Wall
descriptions: Last remaining part of Jerusalem's Second Temple, a holy site of Judaism
Jews tuck slips of paper with prayers into the cracks between the stones
The lowest stones date from the time of King Herod, around 37 BC
The Wall is divided into two sections: men on the left, women on the right
Millions of Jewish pilgrims from around the world come here each year

yad-vashem.name: Yad Vashem
descriptions: World memorial to the six million Jews murdered in the Holocaust
Its Avenue of the Righteous honors non-Jews who saved Jews during the Holocaust
Opened in 1953, it holds the largest archive of victims' names in the world
The main museum is built into the mountain and the route descends into darkness
It welcomes about a million visitors each year in Jerusalem

masjid-al-haram.name: Masjid al-Haram
descriptions: The largest mosque in the world, holding more than 2 million worshippers
It surrounds the Kaaba, the sacred cube regarded as the house of God
Muslims around the world turn toward Mecca to pray
The Hajj, the yearly pilgrimage, brings up to 3 million worshippers to the site
Only Muslims are allowed to enter the city of Mecca

hegra.name: Hegra (Madain Saleh)
descriptions: The first UNESCO World Heritage Site in Saudi Arabia
A Nabatean city with more than 100 monumental tombs carved into sandstone
It was the second most important city of the Nabatean Empire after Petra
Inscriptions on the tombs show the identity and rank of the deceased
It has been a UNESCO World Heritage Site since 2008

burj-khalifa.name: Burj Khalifa
descriptions: The tallest structure ever built by man, at 828 meters
Its construction required 110,000 tons of concrete and 55,000 tons of steel
It houses apartments, offices, an Armani hotel, and an observatory
Up to 12,000 workers were on the construction site each day
Its name honors Khalifa bin Zayed Al Nahyan, president of the UAE

burj-al-arab.name: Burj Al Arab
descriptions: Built on an artificial island 280 meters off the Dubai coast
Its shape recalls the sail of a dhow, a traditional Arab fishing boat
It is often called the only seven-star hotel in the world
Its indoor atrium is the largest in the world at 180 meters tall
Each suite spans two floors with panoramic views of the gulf

mosquee-cheikh-zayed.name: Sheikh Zayed Grand Mosque
descriptions: The third largest mosque in the world, holding 40,000 worshippers
It houses the largest hand-knotted carpet in the world, at 5,627 m²
Its white marble columns are decorated with mother-of-pearl and gold flowers
It was built with marble imported from Italy, India, and Greece
The founder of the UAE, Sheikh Zayed, is buried there

palm-jumeirah.name: Palm Jumeirah
descriptions: An artificial island shaped like a palm tree, visible from space
Its construction required 94 million cubic meters of sand and rock
It added 78 km of coastline to the Emirate of Dubai
Its monorail links the trunk of the palm to the mainland in minutes
The Atlantis hotel sits at the end of the crescent formed by the branches

museum-future.name: Museum of the Future
descriptions: Opened in 2022, named one of the most beautiful buildings in the world
Its steel facade is engraved with Arabic calligraphy of poems by Dubai's ruler
Its toroidal architecture without central pillars is an engineering feat
Its interior presents futuristic visions of technology and humanity
The building is LEED Platinum certified for environmental sustainability

ziggurat-ur.name: Ziggurat of Ur
descriptions: One of the best-preserved ziggurats in Mesopotamia
Built around 2100 BC by King Ur-Nammu to honor the god Nanna
It originally rose over three levels, of which only the first is well preserved
Ur was one of the largest Sumerian cities, with about 65,000 inhabitants
The bricks at the base still bear the names of the kings who built it

ctesiphon.name: Arch of Ctesiphon
descriptions: The largest unreinforced brick arch ever built
Former capital of the Parthian and then Sassanid empires
Its arch is 35 meters tall and 26 meters wide
At its peak it was one of the largest cities in the world
Floods from the Tigris partly destroyed the wings of the palace

baalbek.name: Baalbek
descriptions: Home to the largest Roman temples ever built
The Temple of Jupiter had 54 columns 20 meters tall, only 6 are still standing
Some foundation stones weigh 800 tons, the heaviest ever cut
It was a Phoenician then Hellenistic city before becoming Roman and Byzantine
It has been a UNESCO World Heritage Site since 1984

fort-bahla.name: Bahla Fort
descriptions: The largest fort in Oman, built of mud brick across an area of 12 km²
It was the seat of the powerful Banu Nabhan tribe from the 12th to 15th century
Its dried clay walls are several meters thick
The Bahla oasis has been known for its potters for centuries
It has been a UNESCO World Heritage Site since 1987

registan-samarkand.name: Registan of Samarkand
descriptions: The main square of Samarkand, surrounded by three large madrasahs
Its name means Sandy Place in Persian
Tamerlane made Samarkand the capital of his empire in the 14th century
Its blue ceramic facades are among the most beautiful in Islamic architecture
It has been a UNESCO World Heritage Site since 2001

mausolee-tamerlan.name: Gur-e-Amir (Tamerlane's Mausoleum)
descriptions: Mausoleum of the conqueror Timur, known as Tamerlane, one of history's greatest conquerors
Its 34-meter ribbed dome is covered in turquoise-blue tiles
Legend says that whoever opened his tomb would unleash a terrible war
His tomb was opened by Soviet archaeologists in June 1941, two days before the Nazi invasion
It has been a UNESCO World Heritage Site since 2001

kalon-minaret.name: Kalyan Minaret
descriptions: A 46-meter minaret built in 1127, one of the oldest in Central Asia
Its name means Great Minaret in Tajik
Genghis Khan spared it during his conquest of Bukhara, admiring its beauty
Its brick decoration forms 14 bands of different patterns
It has been a UNESCO World Heritage Site since 1993

erdene-zuu.name: Erdene Zuu Monastery
descriptions: The first Buddhist monastery in Mongolia, founded in 1586 in the ruins of Karakorum
Its 400-meter-long walls are topped with 108 white stupas
It was built with stones taken from the destroyed Mongol capital
At its peak, it housed more than 60 temples and 1,500 monks
It has been a UNESCO World Heritage Site since 2004

tian-tan-buddha.name: Tian Tan Buddha
descriptions: A 34-meter bronze Buddha statue, visible from far out at sea
It shows Buddha Amitabha sitting in lotus position on a lotus flower
Its construction took 12 years and was completed in 1993
It is reached by a staircase of 268 steps from the Po Lin Monastery
It symbolizes harmony between man, nature, and religion

taipei-101.name: Taipei 101
descriptions: It was the tallest building in the world from 2004 to 2010, at 508 meters
Its structure is inspired by bamboo, a symbol of Asian resilience
It contains a 660-ton mass damper to resist typhoons
Its elevators travel 1,010 meters per minute, among the fastest in the world
Its annual New Year fireworks display is famous

ruines-saint-paul-macao.name: Ruins of St. Paul's
descriptions: The Baroque facade of a former Jesuit church, a symbol of Macao
The church was built between 1602 and 1640 by exiled Japanese craftsmen
It was destroyed by a typhoon and a fire in 1835, only the facade remains
The facade has five levels of ornament mixing Western and Eastern art
It has been a UNESCO World Heritage Site since 2005

mosquee-baitul-mukarram.name: Baitul Mukarram Mosque
descriptions: Bangladesh's national mosque, one of the ten largest mosques in the world
Its cube-like design is inspired by the Kaaba in Mecca
It can hold 40,000 worshippers at once
Opened in 1968, it is the center of religious life in Dhaka
Its main minaret reaches 67 meters tall

shat-gombuj-mosque.name: Sixty Dome Mosque
descriptions: The Mosque of Sixty Domes, a treasure of medieval Bengali architecture
Its name comes from its 77 domes, not sixty, despite the popular nickname
Built in the 15th century by Governor Ulugh Khan Jahan
Its walls and columns are made entirely of local terracotta
It has been a UNESCO World Heritage Site since 1985

tigers-nest.name: Tiger's Nest Monastery (Paro Taktsang)
descriptions: Buddhist monastery perched at 3,120 meters on a cliff face
Legend says Guru Rinpoche flew there on the back of a tigress
It is reached by a 5 km hiking trail from the Paro valley
Built in 1692, it was partly destroyed by a fire in 1998
It is the most sacred and most visited site in Bhutan

minaret-djam.name: Minaret of Jam
descriptions: A 12th-century minaret 65 meters tall, lost in a remote valley
It is decorated with epigraphic brick tiles and geometric patterns
It is sometimes identified as the remains of the mythical city of Firuzkuh
It is one of the tallest medieval minarets still standing in the world
It has been a UNESCO World Heritage Site since 2002

pha-that-luang.name: Pha That Luang
descriptions: Laos's national monument, shown on the country's official seal
Its name means Great Sacred Stupa in Lao
Built in the 16th century to house a Buddha relic
The golden spire represents a lotus flower seen from the front
It was destroyed by the Thais in the 19th century and rebuilt in 1935

vat-xiengthong.name: Wat Xieng Thong
descriptions: The most revered temple in Luang Prabang, built in 1560
Its cascading roof, almost touching the ground, is its signature feature
The mosaic tree of life at the back of the temple is a craft masterpiece
The King of Laos was crowned in this temple until 1975
It has been a UNESCO World Heritage Site since 1995

mausolee-khoja-ahmed-yasawi.name: Mausoleum of Khoja Ahmed Yasawi
descriptions: Commissioned by Tamerlane in honor of the Kazakh Sufi poet Khoja Ahmed Yasawi
Its 38.7-meter turquoise dome is the largest of medieval Central Asia
Construction stopped when Tamerlane died and was never fully finished
The mausoleum also includes an assembly hall, a library, and a mosque
It has been a UNESCO World Heritage Site since 2003

juche-tower.name: Juche Tower
descriptions: Monument built to celebrate the 70th birthday of Kim Il-sung
Each side of its base has 25,500 blocks, one for each day of the leader's life
Its eternal flame burns at the top, 170 meters above the ground
Juche is the official ideology of self-reliance in North Korea
The tallest granite tower in the world, according to North Korean sources

krak-des-chevaliers.name: Krak des Chevaliers
descriptions: Considered one of the best-preserved Crusader castles in the world
Held for more than 160 years by the Knights Hospitaller
Its two concentric walls could hold up to 2,000 soldiers
It was never taken by force, only by trickery in 1271
It has been a UNESCO World Heritage Site since 2006

palmyre.name: Palmyra
descriptions: Ancient caravan city nicknamed the Queen of the Desert
It reached its peak under Queen Zenobia in the 3rd century
The Arch of Triumph and the Temple of Bel were destroyed by ISIS in 2015
The main colonnade was 1,100 meters long
It has been a UNESCO World Heritage Site since 1980

longmen.name: Longmen Grottoes
descriptions: More than 100,000 Buddhist statues carved into limestone cliffs
Its construction lasted 400 years, from the 5th to the 9th century
The Fengxian cave holds a seated Buddha 17 meters tall
Statues less than a centimeter tall sit alongside the colossal one
It has been a UNESCO World Heritage Site since 2000

mogao.name: Mogao Caves
descriptions: The largest set of rock-cut Buddhist temples in the world
Its 492 caves contain 45,000 m² of wall paintings
The Hidden Library was discovered there in 1900, holding 50,000 manuscripts
An active pilgrimage site for a thousand years on the Silk Road
It has been a UNESCO World Heritage Site since 1987

tian-anmen.name: Tiananmen Square
descriptions: Gate that symbolizes modern China, leading to the Forbidden City
Mao Zedong's portrait has hung there since 1949
The square in front of it is the largest public square in the world
Its name means Gate of Heavenly Peace in Chinese
The gate was the site of the proclamation of the People's Republic on October 1, 1949

pont-luding.name: Luding Bridge
descriptions: A 100-meter suspension bridge built entirely from iron chains in 1706
It was one of the few crossings over the Dadu River in the steep gorges
The Battle of Luding Bridge in 1935 is a famous episode of Mao's Long March
Its construction required the work of blacksmiths from across the region
This bridge has linked the provinces of Sichuan and Tibet for more than 300 years

pyramides-de-gizeh.name: Pyramids of Giza
descriptions: The only one of the Seven Wonders of the Ancient World still standing
The Great Pyramid contains about 2.3 million blocks
It was the tallest human-made structure for 3,800 years
Built as the tomb of Pharaoh Khufu around 2560 BC
Its sides face the four cardinal directions

sphinx-de-gizeh.name: Great Sphinx of Giza
descriptions: Carved from a single block of limestone 73 meters long
Its nose was likely broken in the Middle Ages, not by Napoleon
The face may represent the pharaoh Khafre
It has watched over the Giza plateau for about 4,500 years
It is the largest statue from the ancient world

pyramide-de-khafre.name: Pyramid of Khafre
descriptions: It looks taller than the Great Pyramid because it stands on higher ground
