Its top still keeps a piece of the original white limestone casing
It stands 136 meters tall, down from 138 originally
Built by Pharaoh Khafre, son of Khufu
Its funerary complex includes the Great Sphinx right next to it

temple-de-louxor.name: Luxor Temple
descriptions: Linked to the temple of Karnak by an avenue 3 kilometers long
One of its obelisks has stood at Place de la Concorde in Paris since 1836
Built mainly by Amenhotep III and Ramesses II
It later housed an Islamic mosque built inside the temple itself
Dedicated to the Theban triad: Amun, Mut, and Khonsu

temple-d-abou-simbel.name: Abu Simbel Temple
descriptions: Ramesses II had four 20-meter colossi carved in his own image
Moved entirely by UNESCO between 1964 and 1968 because of the Aswan Dam
Twice a year, the sun lights up the statues at the back of the sanctuary
It also celebrates Ramesses II's victory at the Battle of Kadesh
Carved directly into the cliff of Nubian pink sandstone

temple-de-philae.name: Philae Temple
descriptions: Dedicated to the goddess Isis, worshipped throughout the Mediterranean world
Moved to a nearby island before the Aswan Dam was filled with water
The last Egyptian temple where hieroglyphs were carved, in 394 AD
It was turned into a Christian church in the 5th century
Its facade lit up at night offers a famous sound and light show

temple-d-hatchepsout.name: Mortuary Temple of Hatshepsut
descriptions: Built by the only female pharaoh to rule ancient Egypt
Its three colonnaded terraces echo the nearby temple of Mentuhotep
Hatshepsut was erased from monuments after her death by her successor
Holds frescoes showing a trading expedition to the Land of Punt
Ranked by architects among the most beautiful monuments of antiquity

obelisque-de-louxor.name: Luxor Obelisk
descriptions: One of two original obelisks, the other stands at Place de la Concorde in Paris
Carved with hieroglyphs celebrating the victories of Ramesses II
It stands nearly 25 meters tall and weighs about 250 tons
Cut from a single block of pink granite from Aswan
Given to France by the viceroy of Egypt Muhammad Ali in 1830

mosquee-mohammed-ali.name: Mosque of Muhammad Ali
descriptions: Nicknamed the Alabaster Mosque due to its precious wall coverings
Its two slender minarets are visible from almost anywhere in Cairo
Inspired by Ottoman architecture, especially Hagia Sophia
Built between 1830 and 1857 under Muhammad Ali Pasha
Holds the tomb of Muhammad Ali in a marble enclosure

pyramides-de-meroe.name: Pyramids of Meroë
descriptions: More than 200 pyramids make up this Nubian burial field
More numerous but smaller than the Egyptian pyramids
Built by the rulers of the Kingdom of Kush
Their pointed tops are steeper than Egypt's pyramids
Some were partly destroyed by a treasure hunter in the 19th century

koutoubia-marrakech.name: Koutoubia Mosque
descriptions: Its 70-meter minaret served as the model for the Giralda in Seville
Built in the 12th century by the Almohads, a powerful Berber dynasty
Its name means 'the mosque of the booksellers' in Arabic
Non-Muslims can only visit it from the outside
Visible from almost everywhere in the medina of Marrakech

hassan-tour.name: Hassan Tower
descriptions: Unfinished minaret of a mosque never completed when the sultan died in 1199
Was meant to reach 86 meters, but stops at 44 meters
Surrounded by 356 broken columns, remains of the prayer hall
Designed by the architect Jabir for Sultan Yaqub Al-Mansur
A UNESCO World Heritage Site along with the neighboring mausoleum

mausolee-mohammed-v.name: Mausoleum of Mohammed V
descriptions: Holds the tombs of King Mohammed V and his sons Hassan II and Moulay Abdallah
A guardian constantly reads the Quran for the royal souls
Built entirely of white marble, with zellige tilework and carved plaster decorations
Open to visitors of all faiths, which is rare for a royal mausoleum
Inaugurated in 1971, several years after the king's death in 1961

kasbah-ait-ben-haddou.name: Ksar of Aït Benhaddou
descriptions: Fortified village of red mud-brick, listed as a UNESCO World Heritage Site
A stop on the old caravan route between the Sahara and Marrakech
Featured in many films including Lawrence of Arabia and Game of Thrones
Built mainly of sun-dried earth
Only a few families still live there all year round

mosquee-hassan-ii.name: Hassan II Mosque
descriptions: Its 210-meter minaret is the tallest in the world
Partly built over the Atlantic Ocean, it can hold 105,000 worshippers
Its transparent glass floor lets you see the sea below
Inaugurated in 1993 for the 60th birthday of King Hassan II
Built in seven years by 6,000 Moroccan craftsmen

medina-de-fes.name: Medina of Fez
descriptions: Largest medieval medina in the world, a UNESCO World Heritage Site
Home to the University of Al-Qarawiyyin, founded in 859, the oldest in the world
Over 9,000 alleys form a car-free maze
Its leather tanneries have been operating using methods thousands of years old
Founded in the 9th century by Idris II, founder of the Idrisid dynasty

bab-mansour.name: Bab Mansour
descriptions: The largest and most ornate of Morocco's gates
Its name means 'gate of the victorious converted renegade' in Arabic
Built under Sultan Moulay Ismail, who made Meknes his capital
Decorated with zellige mosaics and interlaced horseshoe arches
Completed in 1732 by the sultan's son, a year after Moulay Ismail's death

amphitheatre-el-jem.name: Amphitheatre of El Jem
descriptions: Third-largest Roman amphitheater in the world
Could hold 35,000 spectators for gladiator fights
Built without foundations on Tunisian soil around 238 AD
Used by the Berbers as a fortress in the 7th century against the Arabs
Its state of preservation makes it a symbol of Tunisia

ruines-de-carthage.name: Ruins of Carthage
descriptions: Founded around 814 BC by Phoenicians from Tyre
Rival city of Rome, destroyed after the Third Punic War
Hannibal Barca, who almost conquered Rome, was born here around 247 BC
Rebuilt by the Romans, it became the third-largest city of the Empire
Its ruins are a UNESCO World Heritage Site

grande-mosquee-de-kairouan.name: Great Mosque of Kairouan
descriptions: One of the holiest mosques in Islam and the first in Africa
Founded in 670 by Uqba ibn Nafi, the Arab general who conquered the Maghreb
Its square minaret is the oldest minaret still standing in the world
Its columns come from Roman and Byzantine sites across the region
Kairouan was the capital of Islamic North Africa in the 8th and 9th centuries

djemila-ruines.name: Djémila Ruins
descriptions: One of the best-preserved Roman cities in Africa
Its Berber name Djemila means 'the beautiful'
Built at 900 meters altitude in the Algerian mountains
Keeps its forum, baths and triumphal arches in excellent condition
Listed as a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 1982

casbah-d-alger.name: Casbah of Algiers
descriptions: Historic district of Algiers built on a hill overlooking the Mediterranean
Mix of Ottoman Turkish and Moorish architecture
Its narrow alleys sheltered resistance networks during the Algerian War
The Casbah has several Ottoman palaces decorated with ceramic tiles
Listed as a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 1992

leptis-magna.name: Leptis Magna
descriptions: One of the best-preserved Roman cities in the world
Birthplace of Emperor Septimius Severus, who greatly embellished it
Its triumphal arch, baths and forum are still standing
Gradually abandoned after the Arab invasions of the 7th century
Desert sands protected its monuments from erosion for centuries

eglise-saint-georges-lalibela.name: Church of Saint George, Lalibela
descriptions: Carved from a single block of red volcanic rock, 12 meters deep
Built in the 12th century by King Lalibela, who wanted to create an African Jerusalem
Its Greek cross shape is visible from the air
Still used for Orthodox Christian worship today
Lalibela has eleven rock-hewn churches connected by tunnels

obelisque-d-axoum.name: Obelisk of Axum
descriptions: A 24-meter stela carved from a single block of granite, dating to the 4th century
Taken to Italy by Mussolini in 1937, returned to Ethiopia in 2008
Probably marks the tomb of an unidentified Aksumite king
Aksum was the capital of one of the most powerful ancient empires in Africa
A UNESCO World Heritage Site along with the ruins of Aksum

grande-mosquee-de-djenne.name: Great Mosque of Djenné
descriptions: Largest mud-brick (banco) building in the world
Its facade bristling with wooden beams serves as scaffolding during the yearly replastering
The whole village takes part in the big collective replastering each spring
The original was destroyed; the current building dates from 1907 and follows the old shape
The town of Djenne is a UNESCO World Heritage Site

mosquee-djingareyber-tombouctou.name: Djinguereber Mosque
descriptions: Built in 1327 by the Andalusian architect Abu Ishaq es-Saheli
Funded with gold brought back from the pilgrimage to Mecca by Mansa Musa
In the 14th century, Timbuktu was one of the most learned cities in the world
The mosque holds a library of valuable medieval manuscripts
A UNESCO World Heritage Site along with the city's two other mosques

falaises-de-bandiagara.name: Bandiagara Escarpment
descriptions: A 200-kilometer cliff that shelters Dogon villages and granaries perched on its face
The Dogon developed one of the most complex cosmologies in Africa here
The Tellem funeral granaries are carved at dizzying heights
Masked Dogon dancers still perform ancient rituals here
Listed as a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 1989

monument-de-la-renaissance-africaine.name: African Renaissance Monument
descriptions: Largest statue in Africa at 49 meters tall
Shows a man, a woman and a child rising out of a mountain
Built by North Korean workers from the Mansudae Art Studio
Inaugurated in 2010 for the 50th anniversary of Senegal's independence
Inside is a museum reached by elevator

ile-de-goree.name: Gorée Island — House of Slaves
descriptions: An island symbol of the Atlantic slave trade, visited by many heads of state
The House of Slaves and its 'Door of No Return' are iconic landmarks
About 12 million Africans were deported from the Senegalese coast
Today the island is a peaceful car-free village facing Dakar
Listed as a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 1978

kilimanjaro-uhuru-peak.name: Mount Kilimanjaro
descriptions: Highest peak in Africa at 5,895 meters above sea level
Summit of a dormant volcano whose crater still holds glaciers
Its Swahili name probably means 'white mountain'
About 35,000 people try to climb it every year
Visible on clear days from more than 200 kilometers away

fort-jesus-mombasa.name: Fort Jesus
descriptions: Portuguese fortress built to protect the spice route to India
Its six-meter-thick walls withstood many Arab sieges
It changed hands nine times in 300 years between the Portuguese, Arabs and British
Its cross-shaped plan is visible from the air, representing the cross of Christ
Listed as a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 2011

cap-de-bonne-esperance.name: Cape of Good Hope — Lighthouse
descriptions: Lighthouse on the most famous headland of the southern hemisphere
Vasco da Gama sailed past it in 1497, opening the sea route to India
Long believed to be the southernmost point of Africa, which is incorrect
Meeting point of the warm Indian Ocean and cold Atlantic currents
The cape is now at the heart of a protected national park

musee-de-l-apartheid.name: Apartheid Museum
descriptions: The only museum in the world devoted entirely to the history of apartheid
At the entrance, visitors are randomly given a 'white' or 'non-white' card
Opened in 2001 on the site of a former Johannesburg casino
Its archives document 50 years of institutional segregation
Visited by more than a million people each year

union-buildings-pretoria.name: Union Buildings
descriptions: Seat of the presidency of the South African Republic since 1910
Designed by British architect Herbert Baker, commissioned by Louis Botha
Nelson Mandela was sworn in as president here on 10 May 1994, the official end of apartheid
Its two symmetrical wings symbolize the union of British and Boer peoples
The terraced gardens offer panoramic views of Pretoria

robben-island.name: Robben Island Prison
descriptions: Nelson Mandela was imprisoned here for 18 of his 27 years in detention
The island also held a quarantine station and a leper colony in the 19th and 20th centuries
Its former guards and prisoners now serve as tour guides
Listed as a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 1999 as a symbol of freedom
Visible from Cape Town's waterfront, 12 kilometers offshore

grand-zimbabwe.name: Great Zimbabwe
descriptions: Ruins of the capital of a medieval African kingdom, built without mortar or cement
Zimbabwe (the country) takes its name from this site: 'house of stone' in Shona
The Great Enclosure has walls 11 meters high and 5 meters thick
Inhabited from the 11th to the 15th century by up to 18,000 people
Listed as a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 1986

palais-royaux-d-abomey.name: Royal Palaces of Abomey
descriptions: Former capital of the Kingdom of Dahomey, one of the most powerful in West Africa
The bas-reliefs on its palaces tell the story of the kings through symbolic images
Twelve kings reigned here between 1625 and the French conquest in 1894
The Dahomey Amazons, an elite corps of women soldiers, guarded the palaces
Listed as a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 1985

forts-du-ghana-cape-coast.name: Cape Coast Castle
descriptions: One of the largest slave forts on the West African coast
Built by the Swedes in 1653, then passed to the British
Its 'dungeons of death' could imprison 1,000 enslaved people at once
Barack Obama and Michelle Obama visited it in 2009
A UNESCO World Heritage Site along with the nearby Elmina forts

basilique-yamoussoukro.name: Basilica of Our Lady of Peace
descriptions: Largest Christian basilica in the world, exceeding St. Peter's in Rome by area
Built in just three years by President Felix Houphouet-Boigny
Offered as a gift to the Vatican, it was consecrated by John Paul II in 1990
Its 158-meter dome is visible from 20 kilometers around
Can hold 200,000 worshippers, including 18,000 inside

olumo-rock-abeokuta.name: Olumo Rock
descriptions: A 137-meter granite rock that sheltered the Egba people in the 19th century
Its name means 'the rock that stops the enemy' in Yoruba
Natural caves at its base served as shelters during tribal wars
A modern elevator now lets visitors reach the summit
A major cultural and tourist symbol of Ogun State in Nigeria

tombeaux-des-rois-buganda.name: Tombs of Buganda Kings
descriptions: Burial site of the Kabaka kings of the Buganda kingdom since the 19th century
Its thatched tombs are the largest reed structure in Africa
Heavily damaged by an arson attack in 2010, since restored
A sacred pilgrimage site for the Baganda people of Uganda
Listed as a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 2001

memorial-genocide-kigali.name: Kigali Genocide Memorial
descriptions: Holds the remains of more than 250,000 victims of the 1994 genocide
The Tutsi genocide killed between 800,000 and 1 million people in 100 days
Its gardens serve as a final resting place for victims who were found
A permanent exhibition documents the events and their root causes
Inaugurated on 7 April 2004, for the 10th anniversary of the genocide

palais-de-la-reine-antananarivo.name: Queen's Palace (Rova)
descriptions: Residence of the Merina rulers overlooking Antananarivo from its hilltop
Destroyed by fire in 1995, its rebuilding is still ongoing
Symbol of the Kingdom of Madagascar before the French colonization of 1896
Its architecture blends Malagasy traditions and European influences
Surrounded by secondary palaces forming a unique royal complex

musee-national-de-yaounde.name: National Museum of Cameroon
descriptions: Housed in the former presidential palace built during the colonial era
Holds art and ethnology collections from the many peoples of Cameroon
Cameroon is nicknamed 'Africa in miniature' for its cultural diversity
Its tree-lined park is one of the most beautiful green spaces in Yaounde
Opened to the public in 1989 to better share Cameroonian heritage

temple-de-soleb.name: Temple of Soleb
descriptions: Funerary temple of Ramesses II in Nubia, dedicated to himself and the god Amun
Its columns with floral capitals echo the architecture of Luxor
Partly torn down by the Meroites, who reused its columns
Excavated by Italian archaeologists in the 1950s and 1960s
Testifies to Egyptian rule over Nubia during the New Kingdom

temple-de-kom-ombo.name: Temple of Kom Ombo
descriptions: Double temple dedicated to two gods: the falcon Haroeris and the crocodile Sobek
Its symmetrical structure is unique in ancient Egyptian architecture
Mummified crocodiles were found here and are now displayed in the site museum
A medical calendar showing ancient surgical instruments decorates its walls
Built by the Ptolemies in the 2nd and 1st centuries BC

temple-d-edfou.name: Temple of Edfu
descriptions: Best-preserved temple in all of ancient Egypt
Built over 180 years by the Ptolemaic rulers starting in 237 BC
Dedicated to the falcon god Horus, son of Isis and Osiris
Its walls retell the myth of the battle between Horus and Seth
Buried under meters of sand for centuries, it emerged intact

temple-de-medinet-habou.name: Medinet Habu Temple
descriptions: Funerary temple of Ramesses III, the last great warrior pharaoh of Egypt
Its reliefs depict the victory over the Sea Peoples around 1175 BC
The complex is one of the largest and best-preserved in Thebes
A monumental gateway mimics a Syrian stone tower
Love letters carved by workers are inscribed on its columns

colosses-de-memnon.name: Colossi of Memnon
descriptions: Two seated statues 18 meters tall guard the entrance of Amenhotep III's funerary temple
Named after the Trojan hero Memnon by the Greeks, who heard them 'sing'
The sound came from moisture evaporating in the cracks at sunrise
Erected around 1350 BC, they were the largest statues in the world at the time
The temple they guarded, larger than Karnak, has almost entirely disappeared

mosquee-ibn-tulun.name: Mosque of Ibn Tulun
descriptions: Oldest mosque in Cairo still intact, built in 879
Its spiral minaret recalls the minarets of Samarra in Iraq
Its inner courtyard is one of the largest in the Islamic world
Built by Ahmad ibn Tulun, autonomous governor of Abbasid Egypt
Its carved stucco ornaments are among the oldest preserved in Egypt

mosquee-al-azhar.name: Al-Azhar Mosque
descriptions: One of the first mosques in Fatimid Cairo, founded in 972
Home to Al-Azhar University, one of the oldest still active in the world
Global center of Sunni Islamic learning for a thousand years
Several minarets in different styles show its many expansions
Each new ruler of Egypt added his own architectural mark

phare-d-alexandrie.name: Lighthouse of Alexandria (Qaitbay Citadel)
descriptions: Fort Qaitbay, built in 1477 on the site of the famous ancient Lighthouse
The Lighthouse of Alexandria, one of the Seven Wonders of the World, once stood here
Built with blocks from the lighthouse, which collapsed in earthquakes in the 14th century
Sultan Qaitbay's naval defense against Ottoman threats
Its cannons have pointed toward the Mediterranean for more than 500 years

jardins-majorelle-marrakech.name: Majorelle Garden
descriptions: A 1.2-hectare garden created by the French painter Jacques Majorelle starting in 1924
Bought and restored by Yves Saint Laurent and Pierre Berge in 1980
Its villa and pots are painted a cobalt blue called 'Majorelle blue'
Home to more than 300 plant species from all five continents
Yves Saint Laurent's ashes were scattered in the garden in 2008

volubilis-ruines.name: Volubilis Ruins
descriptions: Ancient Roman city whose mosaics are among the best-preserved in Africa
Capital of the province of Mauretania Tingitana in the 2nd century
Its ruins stretch over 43 hectares at the foot of the Middle Atlas
The city was inhabited until the 11th century, long after the fall of Rome
Listed as a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 1997

medina-de-tunis.name: Medina of Tunis
descriptions: Founded in the 7th century, it was one of the great cities of the medieval Islamic world
Its specialized souks (hats, perfumes, jewelry) have been active for centuries
The Zitouna Mosque has been its spiritual heart since the 8th century
More than 700 historic monuments are listed within it
Listed as a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 1979

monastere-de-debre-damo.name: Debre Damo Monastery
descriptions: Monastery founded in the 6th century, reachable only by a leather rope
Perched on an amba (rocky plateau) 800 meters high
Women, both human and animal, have been barred since its founding
Its wooden basilica is the oldest church still standing in Ethiopia
It keeps some of the most valuable illuminated manuscripts in Africa

voortrekker-monument.name: Voortrekker Monument
descriptions: Monument dedicated to the Boer pioneers who left the Cape Colony in the 19th century
Its marble frieze tells the story of the Great Trek of 1838 in 27 bas-reliefs
Each year, at noon on 16 December, a sunbeam lights up the inscription 'Ons vir jou Suid-Afrika'
Inaugurated in 1949, it drew 250,000 people on opening day
Designed by architect Gert Moerdijk, it represents Afrikaner identity

musee-egyptien-du-caire.name: Egyptian Museum of Cairo
descriptions: Largest collection of Egyptian antiquities in the world, with 120,000 objects
Holds the treasures of Tutankhamun's tomb, including his gold mask
Built in 1902 by the French architect Marcel Dourgnon
Its royal mummies include those of Ramesses II and Seti I
It will soon be replaced by the Grand Egyptian Museum in Giza

statue-de-la-liberte.name: Statue of Liberty
descriptions: A gift from France to the United States for the centennial of their independence
Its metal framework was designed by Gustave Eiffel
Its green color comes from the natural oxidation of copper
The 7 points of its crown represent the 7 seas and 7 continents
The tablet it holds shows the date 4 July 1776

empire-state-building.name: Empire State Building
descriptions: It was the tallest building in the world for 40 years
Its construction took only 410 days
It holds 73 elevators across 102 floors
Its top is struck by lightning about 100 times a year
It was inaugurated by President Hoover, who pressed a button from Washington

chrysler-building.name: Chrysler Building
descriptions: It was briefly the tallest building in the world in 1930
Its top with gargoyles draws on Chrysler hubcap designs
The final lift of its spire was done in secret to beat a rival
Built with stainless steel that gleams in the sun
The elevator interiors are decorated with exotic woods and inlays

pont-brooklyn.name: Brooklyn Bridge
descriptions: It was the first suspension bridge to use steel cables
Its construction took 14 years and cost several workers their lives
Its architect John Roebling died before the project was finished
When it opened, it was the longest suspension bridge in the world
About 100,000 vehicles and pedestrians cross it every day

maison-blanche.name: White House
descriptions: It has been the home of every U.S. president since John Adams
It has 132 rooms, 35 bathrooms and 6 floors
It was burned by the British in 1814 during the War of 1812
Its official address is 1600 Pennsylvania Avenue
The president's Oval Office is located in the West Wing

capitole-etats-unis.name: United States Capitol
descriptions: Its dome weighs about 4,000 tons and rises to 87 meters
It houses both chambers of Congress: the Senate and the House of Representatives
The Rotunda is decorated with the fresco 'The Apotheosis of Washington'
Its cornerstone was laid by George Washington in 1793
It was partly burned by the British in 1814

monument-washington.name: Washington Monument
descriptions: At 169 meters, it is the tallest masonry obelisk in the world
You can see a change in stone color about a third of the way up
Its construction was paused for 23 years due to lack of funds
When it opened in 1884, it was the tallest building in the world
It is built of marble, granite and blue gneiss

memorial-lincoln.name: Lincoln Memorial
descriptions: Its statue of Lincoln stands about 5.8 meters tall
Martin Luther King Jr. gave his 'I Have a Dream' speech here in 1963
Its design draws on the temples of ancient Greece
The 36 columns represent the states of the Union when Lincoln died
The words of the Gettysburg Address are carved into the marble

memorial-vietnam.name: Vietnam Veterans Memorial
descriptions: It bears the names of 58,320 American soldiers killed or missing in Vietnam
Its designer Maya Lin was only 21 when she won the competition
The names are engraved in order of date of death
The black granite wall reflects the faces of visitors
It drew more than 5 million visitors in its first year

mount-rushmore.name: Mount Rushmore
descriptions: The faces of the four presidents are each about 18 meters tall
Its sculpture took 14 years, from 1927 to 1941
Over 400 workers took part in its making, with no deaths
Gutzon Borglum, its creator, died a few months before completion
It sits in the Black Hills, sacred to the Lakota Sioux

golden-gate-bridge.name: Golden Gate Bridge
descriptions: Its 'international orange' color was chosen for visibility in fog
It was the longest suspension bridge in the world for 27 years
Its construction required 129,466 kilometers of steel cable
It can stretch up to 2.7 meters in extreme heat
About 10 million people cross it on foot each year

alcatraz.name: Alcatraz Prison
descriptions: It served as a federal prison from 1934 to 1963
It held famous criminals like Al Capone and 'Machine Gun' Kelly
No successful escape has ever been officially confirmed
The current of San Francisco Bay made swimming away very dangerous
It was occupied by Native American activists for 19 months in 1969-1971

hollywood-sign.name: Hollywood Sign
descriptions: Each letter is about 14 meters tall
Originally, the sign read 'Hollywoodland' as a real estate ad
The word 'land' was removed in 1949 during its restoration
It is lit at night and visible from a large part of Los Angeles
A caretaker lived in a house at the base of the sign until the 1970s

willis-tower.name: Willis Tower
descriptions: It was the tallest building in the world from 1973 to 1998
Its original name was Sears Tower, before being renamed in 2009
It has 110 floors and 16,000 windows
Glass balconies called 'The Ledge' jut out over empty space on the 103rd floor
About 25,000 people work there each day

national-mall.name: National Mall
descriptions: It links the Capitol to the Lincoln Memorial over about 3 kilometers
It hosts many historic events, like the March on Washington
The Smithsonian museums lining it are all free
The grand reflection in the Memorial's pool is one of the most photographed images in the U.S.
It draws more than 24 million visitors each year

space-needle.name: Space Needle
descriptions: It was built for the 1962 World's Fair in Seattle
Its rotating restaurant makes a full turn every 47 minutes
Its futuristic shape draws on a flying saucer perched on a rocket
It rises to 184 meters and is built to withstand winds of 320 km/h
A glass outdoor elevator climbs to the top in 43 seconds

gateway-arch.name: Gateway Arch
descriptions: At 192 meters, it is the tallest national monument in the United States
Its shape is an inverted catenary, the most stable curve in architecture
A small interior tram carries visitors to the top
Its architect Eero Saarinen died before its construction
It represents the gateway to the West, recalling American expansion

hoover-dam.name: Hoover Dam
descriptions: Its construction required 3.4 million cubic meters of concrete, enough to link New York to San Francisco
It was built during the Great Depression by 21,000 workers
When it opened in 1936, it was the largest dam in the world
It sits on the border between Nevada and Arizona
Its hydroelectric plant powers Las Vegas, Los Angeles and Phoenix

grand-canyon-skywalk.name: Grand Canyon Skywalk
descriptions: It hangs over the Grand Canyon about 1,200 meters above the Colorado River
Its transparent glass floor gives a dizzying view straight down
It is run by the Hualapai tribe on their ancestral lands
Its horseshoe-shaped structure extends 21 meters out over empty space
Visitors must wear special shoe covers to avoid scratching the glass

independence-hall.name: Independence Hall
descriptions: This is where the Declaration of Independence and the U.S. Constitution were signed
Its tower has held the famous Liberty Bell since 1753
It is listed as a UNESCO World Heritage Site
Its distinctive red bricks make it one of the most recognizable buildings in the United States
George Washington, Thomas Jefferson and Benjamin Franklin met here

notre-dame-new-orleans.name: St. Louis Cathedral, New Orleans
descriptions: It is the oldest Catholic cathedral still in use in the United States
It overlooks the famous Jackson Square in the French Quarter
Its white facade is an iconic symbol of New Orleans
It has been destroyed and rebuilt several times since the 17th century
Jazz funerals traditionally start from its steps

grace-cathedral-sf.name: Grace Cathedral
descriptions: It is built on the site of the former home of the very rich Charles Crocker
Its bronze doors are copies of the Gates of Paradise from the Florence Baptistery
It has a meditation labyrinth modeled on the one at Chartres Cathedral
Its construction began after the 1906 earthquake and took decades
It hosts ecumenical services blending music, meditation and the arts

flatiron-building.name: Flatiron Building
descriptions: Its nickname 'Flatiron' comes from its triangular shape, like a clothes iron
It was one of the first skyscrapers in New York when it was built
Its narrowest corner is only 2 meters wide
It was seen as a wild architectural challenge in its day
It has become one of the most photographed buildings in New York

met-museum.name: Metropolitan Museum of Art
descriptions: It is one of the largest art museums in the world with more than 2 million works
Its collection spans 5,000 years of human history across every continent
It draws more than 6 million visitors each year
Its main entrance on Fifth Avenue is a New York icon
Its Egyptian department houses an entire temple: the Temple of Dendur

pentagon.name: The Pentagon
descriptions: It is the largest office building in the world at 600,000 square meters
Its 5 identical sides give it its iconic pentagonal shape
About 23,000 military and civilian staff work there every day
It has its own zip code and its own medical center
Its construction took just 16 months during World War II

liberty-bell.name: Liberty Bell
descriptions: Its famous crack appeared on the very first test ringing in 1753
The inscription on the bell quotes a Bible verse: 'Proclaim liberty'
It originally weighed about 907 kilograms
It was used to announce the first public reading of the Declaration of Independence
It has been on display at the Liberty Bell Center in Philadelphia since 2003

boston-old-state-house.name: Old State House
descriptions: It is the oldest surviving public building in Boston, built in 1713
The Boston Massacre of 1770 took place right outside its doors
The Declaration of Independence was first read publicly in Boston from here
For a long time it was the seat of the British colonial government of Massachusetts
Today it is surrounded by skyscrapers, creating a striking contrast

times-square.name: Times Square
descriptions: It is nicknamed 'the crossroads of the world' for its nonstop activity
Its glowing ball drops every 31 December since 1907 to mark the New Year
It is one of the busiest shopping areas in the world
Giant lit-up advertising boards make it unique at night
About 50 million tourists visit it each year

rockefeller-center.name: Rockefeller Center
descriptions: Its lit-up Christmas tree is one of the most famous traditions in New York
The Rockefeller Center ice rink draws millions of visitors each winter
It is made up of 19 commercial buildings built in the 1930s
Its top, known as '30 Rock', offers one of the best views of Manhattan
The complex houses NBC and several television studios

us-supreme-court.name: United States Supreme Court
descriptions: Its pediment bears the inscription 'Equal Justice Under Law'
It is built of white marble from Vermont, Georgia and Alabama
It was only built in 1935, long after the country's founding
Its 16 Corinthian columns represent the dignity of the law
The 9 justices serve for life once nominated by the president

chateau-frontenac.name: Château Frontenac
descriptions: It is the most photographed hotel in the world, according to the Guinness Book of Records
It rises over Quebec City's Upper Town from its promontory
Its medieval-castle silhouette makes it a symbol of French Canada
It was built by the Canadian Pacific Railway to attract tourists
Winston Churchill and Franklin Roosevelt met here during the Quebec Conferences

tour-cn.name: CN Tower
descriptions: It was the tallest free-standing structure in the world from 1976 to 2007
It rises to 553 meters and overlooks Lake Ontario
Its glass floor at 342 meters lets you look straight down
It is struck by lightning an average of 75 times a year
Its broadcast antenna sends and receives radio and TV signals for Toronto

parliament-canada.name: Parliament of Canada
descriptions: Its Peace Tower houses the carillon and burns the parliamentary flame
The central building was destroyed by fire in 1916 and rebuilt
Its neo-Gothic library is one of the most beautiful in North America
It is the seat of the Senate, the House of Commons and the prime minister's office
Its Gothic Revival architecture recalls the Palace of Westminster

notre-dame-montreal.name: Notre-Dame Basilica of Montreal
descriptions: Its interior is entirely painted in night blue and gilded with gold leaf
Celine Dion was married here in 1994 in front of 500 guests
Its Casavant organ has 7,000 pipes
It can seat more than 3,200 worshippers
Its construction in 1829 made it one of the largest churches in North America

vieux-port-montreal.name: Old Port of Montreal
descriptions: It is one of the oldest districts of Montreal, founded in 1611 by Champlain
Its 19th-century warehouses have been turned into lofts and galleries
The Old Port skating rink is one of the longest outdoor rinks in the world
It runs along the Saint Lawrence River for 2.5 kilometers
Each summer, cruise ships make a stop here

banff-chateau-lake-louise.name: Chateau Lake Louise
descriptions: It is surrounded by glaciers and overlooks the turquoise waters of Lake Louise
Its terrace is one of the most photographed spots in Canada
It sits in Banff National Park, at the heart of the Canadian Rockies
The turquoise water comes from glacial sediment
It has hosted royalty, celebrities and presidents for over a century

rideau-canal.name: Rideau Canal
descriptions: It is listed as a UNESCO World Heritage Site as a masterpiece of engineering
Its construction was ordered after the War of 1812 to link Ottawa to Kingston
In winter, it becomes the longest skating rink in the world at 7.8 km
It was dug between 1826 and 1832 mostly by Irish immigrants
It was never used for military purposes, as originally planned

vieux-quebec-fortifications.name: Fortifications of Quebec
descriptions: Quebec City is the only fortified city north of Mexico in North America
Its ramparts stretch 4.6 kilometers around the Upper Town
It has been listed as a UNESCO World Heritage Site since 1985
The Citadelle of Quebec is still an active military garrison
The fortifications were built by the French and later strengthened by the British

chichen-itza.name: Chichén Itzá
descriptions: The El Castillo pyramid is a stone calendar: 365 steps in total
During the equinoxes, a serpent of light appears to descend the pyramid
The city was abandoned and later rediscovered by the Spanish in the 16th century
Its sacred well was used for Mayan ritual sacrifices
It has been listed among the New Seven Wonders of the World since 2007

teotihuacan.name: Teotihuacán
descriptions: The Pyramid of the Sun is the third largest pyramid in the world
At the start of the common era, it was one of the largest cities in the world with 150,000 inhabitants
Its Nahuatl name means 'the place where men become gods'
The Avenue of the Dead aligns the main pyramids over more than 2 kilometers
Its civilization mysteriously vanished in the 7th century without any known explanation

palacio-bellas-artes.name: Palacio de Bellas Artes
descriptions: Its white marble dome is an icon of Mexico City's historic center
It houses the largest murals by Diego Rivera, Orozco, and Siqueiros
Its construction began in 1904 and was not completed until 1934
Its floor has sunk 4 meters since construction due to Mexico City's soft soil
It blends Art Nouveau on the exterior with Art Deco on the interior

catedral-metropolitana-mexico.name: Mexico City Metropolitan Cathedral
descriptions: It is the largest Catholic cathedral in Latin America
Its construction spanned nearly 250 years, from 1573 to 1813
It is built upon the ruins of the Aztec Great Temple
It tilts slightly because Mexico City rests on a former dried-up lake
It has 5 naves, 16 chapels, and 16 bells in its two towers

zocalo-mexico.name: Zócalo
descriptions: It is one of the largest public squares in the world at 57,600 m²
It was the ceremonial center of the ancient Aztec Tenochtitlan
Its Mexican flag is one of the largest ever raised in a public square
The National Palace and the Metropolitan Cathedral border it
It hosts major national celebrations, including Independence Day on September 15

palenque.name: Palenque
descriptions: Its bas-reliefs are among the finest examples of classic Mayan art
King Pakal's sarcophagus was discovered here in 1952, an archaeological masterpiece
The city is surrounded by dense jungle at the foot of the Chiapas hills
Less than 10% of the city has been excavated: thousands of structures remain hidden
It was abandoned around 900 AD for reasons still poorly understood

monte-alban.name: Monte Albán
descriptions: It is one of the first great Mesoamerican cities, founded around 500 BC
It was the capital of the Zapotec civilization for over 1,000 years
Its location on a flattened summit offers a panoramic view of the three Oaxaca valleys
Its tombs adorned with frescoes and ceramics yielded priceless treasures
One of its buildings is oriented unusually: it likely served as an observatory

uxmal.name: Uxmal
descriptions: The Pyramid of the Magician was reportedly built in a single night according to Mayan legend
It is famous for the ornamental beauty of its stone mosaic facade
Unlike other sites, Uxmal has no well: rainwater was collected in cisterns
The Nunnery Quadrangle is a masterpiece of Mayan architecture
Its buildings are covered with masks of Chaac, the rain god

tulum.name: Tulum
descriptions: It is one of the few Mayan cities built on the shore of the Caribbean Sea
Its ruins overlook a cliff 12 meters above the turquoise water
It served as both a trading port and a ceremonial center
The frescoes in its Temple of the Diving God are remarkably well preserved
It is the most visited archaeological site in Mexico with 2 million visitors per year

pyramide-cholula.name: Great Pyramid of Cholula
descriptions: It is the largest pyramid in the world by volume, larger than Khufu
It measures 55 meters in height and 450 meters per side at the base
The Spanish built a church on top without knowing it was a pyramid
It is made up of four superimposed pyramids built over several centuries
A network of 8 kilometers of tunnels allows exploration of its inner layers

castillo-chapultepec.name: Chapultepec Castle
descriptions: It is the only castle in North America to have housed a serving head of state
It served as the residence of Emperor Maximilian I of Mexico in the 19th century
It now houses the National Museum of History of Mexico
Military cadets heroically defended the fortress against American troops in 1847
It is perched on a volcanic rock in the middle of Chapultepec Park

tikal.name: Tikal
descriptions: Its temples rise from the Guatemalan jungle canopy like stone needles
In the 5th century, Tikal was one of the most powerful Mayan cities with 50,000 inhabitants
Its forest setting was used as the backdrop for the planet Yavin in Star Wars
Temple I, known as the 'Temple of the Great Jaguar,' rises to 47 meters
It was rediscovered by Westerners in 1848 after centuries of obscurity

copan.name: Copán
descriptions: Its sculpted stelae and altars are the finest in the entire Mayan world
The Hieroglyphic Stairway is the longest known Mayan text with 2,500 glyphs
Copán was the great intellectual and artistic center of the Mayan civilization
Its ruins are located in the Honduran jungle near the Guatemalan border
Recent excavations have revealed dozens of structures still buried

antigua-guatemala.name: Antigua Guatemala
descriptions: Its ruins of colonial convents and churches are listed by UNESCO
It was the capital of Spanish Central America until the 1773 earthquake
Its cobbled streets and colonial fountains give it the atmosphere of a 17th-century town
It is framed by three volcanoes: Agua, Fuego, and Acatenango
Its Holy Week processions are among the most followed in the world

fort-san-lorenzo.name: Caribbean Coast Fortifications
descriptions: These 16th-century Spanish colonial fortifications are listed by UNESCO
They protected the gold and silver route between South America and Spain
Pirate Henry Morgan stormed them in 1671 before sacking Panama
They are located at the mouth of the Chagres River on the Caribbean Sea
Their state of preservation shows Spanish military engineering

cathedral-antigua.name: Cathedral of Santiago de Guatemala
descriptions: Its ruined Baroque facade is the most iconic image of Antigua
It was destroyed by an earthquake in 1773 and never fully rebuilt
It is dedicated to the apostle Saint James, patron saint of Spain
Behind the preserved facade lie the remains of the collapsed main nave
Underground excavations have revealed the tombs of Spanish conquistadors

teatro-nacional-costa-rica.name: National Theatre of Costa Rica
descriptions: It was funded by a tax on exported coffee, the country's main source of wealth
Its construction required materials and craftsmen brought in from Europe
Its painted ceiling depicts the sugar cane and coffee harvest in Costa Rica
It is considered the most beautiful and important building in Costa Rica
It hosts the National Symphony Orchestra and international productions

cahal-pech.name: Cahal Pech
descriptions: Its name means 'place of ticks' in Yucatec Mayan
It is one of the oldest Mayan sites in Belize, inhabited since 1200 BC
It is perched on a hill overlooking the town of San Ignacio
Its 34 structures include temples, palaces, and steam baths
Excavations have uncovered rich funerary offerings including jade and ceramics

xunantunich.name: Xunantunich
descriptions: Its main temple 'El Castillo' rises to 40 meters, the second tallest structure in Belize
Its Mayan name means 'the stone woman' after a local legend
It overlooks the Mopan River valley near the Guatemalan border
Its stucco friezes depict Mayan deities and celestial masks
It is reached by crossing the river on a hand-cranked cable ferry

catedral-havana.name: Havana Cathedral
descriptions: Its Baroque facade is considered the finest in the Americas
It was built by the Jesuits and completed by the Church after their expulsion
It housed the remains of Christopher Columbus for two centuries
Its square surrounded by colonial palaces is one of the most beautiful in Cuba
Its two asymmetrical towers give it a unique character

vieille-havane.name: Old Havana
descriptions: Its colonial alleyways, squares, and Baroque buildings are listed by UNESCO
It was founded by the Spanish in 1519 under the name San Cristóbal de La Habana
Its 1950s American cars have become a symbol of Cuba
Havana's Capitol, built in 1929, resembles the one in Washington
More than 3,000 historic monuments dot its 4.5 km²

fort-christophe-haiti.name: Citadelle Laferrière
descriptions: It is the largest fortress in the Western Hemisphere with an area of 10,000 m²
It was built to defend Haiti against a possible French reconquest
It is perched at 900 meters altitude in the mountains of northern Haiti
Its 5-meter-thick walls could withstand all cannons of the time
It is listed as a UNESCO World Heritage Site

vieille-ville-san-juan.name: Old San Juan
descriptions: San Juan was the second city founded by Europeans in the Americas
Its historic center is paved with bluish cobblestones brought as ballast in Spanish ships
The old town is surrounded by walls built to protect the treasures of the New World
Its brightly colored colonial houses make for a picturesque setting
It is listed as a UNESCO World Heritage Site

catedral-santo-domingo.name: Cathedral of Santa María la Menor
descriptions: It is the oldest completed cathedral in the Western Hemisphere
Its construction began in 1512, only 20 years after Columbus's arrival
It was long thought to hold the remains of Christopher Columbus
Its architecture blends late Gothic, Spanish Plateresque, and Renaissance
It is listed as a UNESCO World Heritage Site along with the colonial city of Santo Domingo

alcazar-colon.name: Alcázar de Colón
descriptions: It is the oldest European residence still standing in the New World
It was built by Diego Columbus, son of Christopher Columbus, around 1510
Its Mudéjar architecture reflects the Arab influence in colonial Spain
It overlooks the mouth of the Ozama River from its promontory
It is listed as a UNESCO World Heritage Site

temple-salt-lake-city.name: Salt Lake Temple
descriptions: Its construction took 40 years and was completed without modern machinery
It is one of the most important temples of The Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints
Its six spires rise to 77 meters in the heart of Salt Lake City
It is built of white granite quarried from the nearby Wasatch Mountains
Only practicing Church members may enter the interior

water-tower-chicago.name: Chicago Water Tower
descriptions: It is one of the few buildings to have survived the Great Chicago Fire of 1871
Its medieval tower of yellow limestone has become a symbol of Chicago's rebuilding
It was built to supply the city with drinking water from Lake Michigan
It is listed as a Chicago Historic Landmark
It never fulfilled its original purpose: it was quickly replaced by newer facilities

musee-air-espace-washington.name: National Air and Space Museum
descriptions: It is the most visited museum in Washington D.C. with more than 9 million visitors per year
Its collection includes over 60,000 artifacts related to the history of aviation and space
It houses the Apollo 11 lunar module and the capsule from the first American space station
It is entirely free like all Smithsonian museums
It opened on July 4, 1976, for the American bicentennial

harvard-university.name: Harvard University
descriptions: It is the oldest university in the United States, founded in 1636
It is named after John Harvard, its first benefactor
Its Widener Library is one of the largest university libraries in the world
Its alumni include 8 U.S. presidents and 160 Nobel laureates
Its $50 billion endowment makes it the wealthiest university in the world

pentagon-memorial.name: Pentagon Memorial
descriptions: It honors the 184 victims of the September 11, 2001 attack on the Pentagon
Each bench bears the name of a victim and is oriented according to their age
It includes 184 illuminated benches arranged by chronological order of birth
It is located at the exact spot where the plane struck the building
A tree is planted behind each bench to symbolize life carrying on

musee-de-young-san-francisco.name: de Young Museum
descriptions: It is housed in a copper and zinc shell that will change color over time
Its perforated copper facade creates shifting light patterns throughout the day
It is one of the most visited art museums in San Francisco
It holds an important collection of African, Oceanic, and Native American art
Its surrounding gardens form an open-air botanical museum

san-francisco-city-hall.name: San Francisco City Hall
descriptions: Its dome surpasses that of the Washington Capitol by about 1.5 meters
It was built after the 1906 earthquake to replace the destroyed building
Its Corinthian columns and Beaux-Arts dome make it a Neoclassical masterpiece
Harvey Milk was assassinated here in 1978 in his office as city supervisor
It is regularly used as a filming location for Hollywood productions

universite-notre-dame.name: University of Notre Dame
descriptions: Its gilded Golden Dome is one of the most recognizable symbols in the United States
Its Basilica of the Sacred Heart is decorated with mosaics and religious art
It is famous for its American football team, 'The Fighting Irish'
Touchdown Jesus, a 20-meter mural on the library, is a pop culture landmark
It is home to one of the largest Catholic libraries in the world

fremont-street.name: Fremont Street Experience
descriptions: Its 460-meter-long LED ceiling is the largest LED screen in the world
It was unveiled in 1995 to revitalize old Las Vegas against the new casinos
More than 12 million LEDs make up its animated ceiling
Sound and light shows are projected on it every hour in the evening
It was Las Vegas's main street before the rise of the Strip

memphis-pyramid.name: Memphis Pyramid
descriptions: This glass and steel pyramid stands 98 meters tall
It was built in tribute to Memphis, a city named after the ancient Egyptian capital
It was transformed in 2015 into a mega Bass Pro Shops store and luxury hotel
Its transparent elevator rises to a hotel suspended high inside the pyramid
Its glass facade reflects the sky and the Mississippi River throughout the day

machu-picchu.name: Machu Picchu
descriptions: An Incan city perched at about 2,430 meters altitude
Built in the 15th century under the emperor Pachacutec
It remained unknown to the Spanish conquistadors
Revealed to the world by Hiram Bingham in 1911
Listed among the new seven wonders of the world

coricancha.name: Coricancha
descriptions: Temple of the Sun, the most sacred religious building of the Incas
Its walls were once covered with gold plates
The Spanish built a convent over its foundations
Its Incan architecture still impresses with its precision
Dedicated to Inti, the sun god revered by the Incas

sacsayhuaman.name: Sacsayhuamán
descriptions: An Incan fortress overlooking the city of Cusco
Its stone blocks weigh up to 300 tons
Assembled without mortar with disconcerting precision
It was the setting of fierce clashes during the Spanish conquest
Its name means 'satisfied falcon' in Quechua

lignes-de-nazca.name: Nazca Lines
descriptions: Gigantic geoglyphs traced in the Peruvian desert
Some figures measure several hundred meters long
Clearly visible only from the air
Their origin and purpose remain partly mysterious
The hummingbird and the spider are among the most famous designs

chan-chan.name: Chan Chan
descriptions: The largest adobe city in the pre-Columbian world
Capital of the Chimú kingdom between the 9th and 15th centuries
Conquered by the Incas around 1470
Its earthen walls are decorated with geometric friezes
Listed as a UNESCO World Heritage Site since 1986

huaca-del-sol.name: Huaca del Sol
descriptions: A huge adobe pyramid built by the Moche people
Constructed with about 143 million adobe bricks
Used as a royal residence and ceremonial site
Partially destroyed by the Spanish in their search for gold
One of the largest pre-Hispanic structures in South America

cathedrale-de-lima.name: Lima Cathedral
descriptions: Baroque cathedral overlooking Lima's Plaza Mayor
Its construction began in 1535, the year the city was founded
It houses the tomb of conquistador Francisco Pizarro
Damaged several times by earthquakes over the centuries
Its interior holds a remarkable collection of colonial paintings

christ-redempteur.name: Christ the Redeemer
descriptions: Colossal 38-meter-tall statue overlooking Rio de Janeiro
Inaugurated in 1931 atop Corcovado mountain
Sculpted by Frenchman Paul Landowski
Listed among the new seven wonders of the world in 2007
Its outstretched arms span 28 meters wide

pain-de-sucre.name: Sugarloaf Mountain
descriptions: Granite rock formation rising 396 meters high
Its name recalls the shape of refined sugar loaves
Accessible by two cable cars since 1912
Iconic symbol of Guanabara Bay in Rio
Listed as a UNESCO World Heritage Site

cathedrale-metropolitaine-rio.name: Metropolitan Cathedral of Rio de Janeiro
descriptions: An unconventional cathedral shaped like a truncated pyramid
Its construction spans from 1964 to 1979
It can hold up to 20,000 people
Its four colorful stained-glass windows, 65 meters tall, are striking
Designed by architect Edgar de Oliveira da Fonseca

theatre-amazonas.name: Amazon Theatre
descriptions: Baroque opera house built in the heart of the Amazon rainforest
Inaugurated in 1896 during the rubber boom
Its colorful dome is covered with French tiles
All materials were imported from Europe
Made famous by Werner Herzog's film Fitzcarraldo

inhotim.name: Inhotim Institute
descriptions: A vast open-air contemporary art park unique in the world
Founded by patron Bernardo Paz on 5,000 hectares
Houses permanent works by nearly 500 artists
The pavilions are set within lush tropical vegetation
One of the largest open-air museums on the planet

pelourinho-salvador.name: Pelourinho
descriptions: Historic colonial center of Salvador de Bahia
Founded in the 16th century as Brazil's first capital
Its colorful facades reflect tropical Baroque architecture
Heart of Afro-Brazilian culture and Candomblé
Listed as a UNESCO World Heritage Site since 1985

ponte-juscelino-kubitschek.name: Juscelino Kubitschek Bridge
descriptions: A bridge spanning Lake Paranoá in Brasília
Its three asymmetrical arches evoke the movement of water
Designed by architect Alexandre Chan and inaugurated in 2002
Lit up at night, it becomes a symbol of modernity
It honors Juscelino Kubitschek, the founding president of Brasília

obelisque-buenos-aires.name: Obelisk of Buenos Aires
descriptions: Iconic monument in the heart of the 9 de Julio Avenue
Built in just 31 days in 1936
Standing 67.5 meters tall, it commemorates the founding of Buenos Aires
The avenue where it rises is one of the widest in the world
A popular gathering spot during Argentine sports victories

casa-rosada.name: Casa Rosada
descriptions: Argentine presidential palace recognizable by its pink facade
Its color is said to come from a mix of limewash and ox blood
From its balcony, Juan Perón addressed the crowds
It houses the president's office but not his official residence
Built on the foundations of a former colonial fortress

theatre-colon-buenos-aires.name: Teatro Colón
descriptions: Considered among the five best opera houses in the world
Inaugurated in 1908 after twenty years of construction
Its main hall can hold 2,500 spectators
Musicians praise its acoustics
Enrico Caruso and Arturo Toscanini both performed here

cathedrale-metropolitaine-ba.name: Buenos Aires Metropolitan Cathedral
descriptions: Main Catholic cathedral of Buenos Aires
Neoclassical facade inspired by the Panthéon in Paris
Houses the mausoleum of General José de San Martín
Jorge Bergoglio, the future Pope Francis, served as its archbishop
Its construction spanned more than two centuries

perito-moreno.name: Perito Moreno Glacier
descriptions: A 250 km² glacier in Argentine Patagonia
One of the few glaciers in the world that is still advancing
Its ice blocks regularly crash into Lake Argentino
Standing 60 to 70 meters above the surface of the lake
Listed as a UNESCO World Heritage Site since 1981

iguazu-falls-argentina.name: Iguazu Falls (Argentine side)
descriptions: A system of 275 waterfalls stretching over 2.7 km
The Devil's Throat, the widest, reaches 150 meters
Wider than Niagara Falls
Eleanor Roosevelt reportedly said 'Poor Niagara!' upon seeing them
Listed as a UNESCO World Heritage Site on both the Argentine and Brazilian sides

moai-ile-de-paques.name: Easter Island Moai
descriptions: Monumental statues carved by the Rapa Nui people
About 900 moai spread across the entire island
Most face inland to protect the villages
The largest standing moai measures 10 meters tall
The island is the most isolated inhabited place on the planet

gran-torre-santiago.name: Gran Torre Santiago
descriptions: Tallest tower in Latin America at 300 meters
Opened in 2013, it dominates the Las Condes financial district
Designed by American architect César Pelli
It includes offices, a hotel, apartments, and a shopping center
Visible from nearly every neighborhood in Santiago

palacio-de-la-moneda.name: La Moneda Palace
descriptions: Former Spanish royal mint turned presidential palace
Designed by Italian architect Joaquín Toesca in the late 18th century
Bombed during the military coup of September 11, 1973
Restored and reopened to the public in 1981
Its basement houses a cultural center open to the public free of charge

fort-valdivia.name: Colonial Forts of Valdivia
descriptions: The best-preserved Spanish colonial fortified complex in the Americas
Built starting in the 17th century to defend the Pacific coast
It consists of six forts spread around Corral Bay
Showcases the bastioned military architecture of the era
Listed as a UNESCO World Heritage Site since 2023

ciudad-perdida.name: Ciudad Perdida (Lost City)
descriptions: A city founded by the Tayrona people around 800 AD
Older than Machu Picchu by about 650 years
Lost in the jungle until its rediscovery in 1972
Reachable only by a four-to-six-day hike
Known as Teyuna by the local indigenous communities

cathedrale-de-sel-zipaquira.name: Salt Cathedral of Zipaquirá
descriptions: A cathedral built 180 meters underground inside a salt mine
It can hold 10,000 worshippers in its underground naves
The first version dated from 1954; the current one from 1995
The pillars and sculptures are carved directly into the salt rock
One of the most visited tourist attractions in Colombia

fort-san-felipe-carthagene.name: Castillo San Felipe de Barajas
descriptions: The largest and most powerful Spanish fortification in the Americas
Built on San Lázaro hill starting in 1536
It repelled attacks by Francis Drake and Baron de Pointis
Its network of underground tunnels enabled secret communications
Listed as a UNESCO World Heritage Site along with the fortifications of Cartagena

murailles-de-carthagene.name: Walls of Cartagena
descriptions: A system of colonial fortifications surrounding the historic center
Construction began in 1586 after Drake's sack
It stretches about 11 kilometers around the old city
Among the best preserved in South America
Listed as a UNESCO World Heritage Site since 1984

tiwanaku.name: Tiwanaku
descriptions: The former capital of a pre-Columbian Andean empire
Founded around 1500 BC on the shore of Lake Titicaca
It reached its peak between 500 and 900 AD
Major spiritual center that inspired the Incas
Listed as a UNESCO World Heritage Site since 2000

porte-du-soleil.name: Gate of the Sun
descriptions: A monolith carved from a single ten-ton block of andesite
Nearly 3 meters tall, it stands at the ancient city of Tiwanaku
Its upper frieze depicts the sun god Viracocha
Its exact function (portal, calendar, altar) remains debated
Moved from its original location, probably in the 19th century

cerro-rico-potosi.name: Cerro Rico of Potosí
descriptions: A mountain nicknamed 'the mountain that eats men'
Discovered in 1545, it was the richest silver mine in the world
It fueled the Spanish colonial economy for two centuries
Millions of forced laborers died in its tunnels
Listed as a UNESCO World Heritage Site since 1987

mitad-del-mundo.name: Mitad del Mundo Monument
descriptions: A monument marking the location of the Earth's equator
Built in 1982, it rises 30 meters tall
Topped by a 4.5-ton globe
Experiments related to the Coriolis effect are demonstrated here
Modern GPS shows that it is slightly off from the true equator line

cathedrale-metropolitaine-quito.name: Quito Metropolitan Cathedral
descriptions: One of the oldest cathedrals in South America
Its construction began in 1535, at the founding of Quito
It blends Gothic, Baroque, and Mudéjar styles in its decoration
It houses paintings from the Quito School, a colonial artistic movement
It is part of the historic center listed as a UNESCO World Heritage Site

eglise-de-la-compagnie-de-jesus-quito.name: Church of the Society of Jesus
descriptions: Considered the masterpiece of Baroque art in Latin America
Its carved stone facade is a true stone lacework
Its construction took 160 years, from 1605 to 1765
The interior is reportedly covered with seven tons of gold
Listed with the historic center of Quito as a UNESCO World Heritage Site

angel-falls.name: Angel Falls
descriptions: The world's tallest waterfall with 979 meters of free fall
Discovered by American aviator Jimmy Angel in 1933
It drops from the Auyán-tepui plateau into the Venezuelan jungle
The water partly vaporizes before reaching the bottom of the falls
Listed as a UNESCO World Heritage Site as part of Canaima National Park

teatro-solis.name: Teatro Solís
descriptions: The oldest and largest opera house in Uruguay
Inaugurated in 1856, it was the country's first opera house
Fully renovated between 2004 and 2009
Its acoustics are praised
Named after Juan Díaz de Solís, the discoverer of the Río de la Plata

ruines-jesuites-trinidad.name: Jesuit Ruins of Trinidad
descriptions: Ruins of a former Jesuit reduction founded in 1706
One of the largest Jesuit missions in Paraguay
Abandoned after the expulsion of the Jesuits in 1768
The main church could hold more than 2,000 worshippers
Listed as a UNESCO World Heritage Site since 1993

opera-de-sydney.name: Sydney Opera House
descriptions: Its Danish architect Jørn Utzon resigned before construction was completed
Its white sails evoke seashells or sailboats
Inaugurated by Queen Elizabeth II in 1973
Covered with more than a million ceramic tiles
Listed as a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 2007

harbour-bridge-sydney.name: Sydney Harbour Bridge
descriptions: Nicknamed 'The Coathanger' for its arch shape
Its construction took eight years and employed 1,400 workers
The steel arch weighs about 39,000 tons
Visitors can climb the arch to enjoy the view
It links downtown Sydney to the North Shore

uluru.name: Uluru (Ayers Rock)
descriptions: This sacred Anangu monolith stands 348 meters tall
Its color shifts from bright red to orange depending on the time of day
Climbing to the top has been banned since 2019 out of cultural respect
It has been listed as a UNESCO World Heritage Site since 1987
The Anangu consider Uluru the spiritual center of the world

douze-apotres.name: Twelve Apostles
descriptions: These limestone formations rise 45 meters above the ocean
Only eight remain, despite the evocative name
Marine erosion regularly destroys these ancient columns
They were formed about 10 to 20 million years ago
The Great Ocean Road runs along this rugged Australian coast

parliament-house-canberra.name: Parliament House
descriptions: It is partially buried beneath Capital Hill
Its roof is topped by an 81-meter stainless steel flagpole
The building contains more than 4,500 Australian artworks
It opened on May 9, 1988, during the Australian bicentennial
The building covers 32 hectares and has 4,700 rooms

australian-war-memorial.name: Australian War Memorial
descriptions: It honors the more than 102,000 Australians killed in combat
Its architecture draws inspiration from Byzantine and Romanesque styles
The flame of remembrance burns permanently in the sanctuary
Inaugurated in 1941 during the Second World War
Its integrated museum is one of the largest military museums in the world

shrine-of-remembrance-melbourne.name: Shrine of Remembrance
descriptions: Built in tribute to Victorian soldiers of the First World War
Each November 11 at 11 a.m., a ray of sunlight illuminates the Stone of Remembrance
Its style is inspired by the Parthenon in Athens and the Mausoleum of Halicarnassus
It is surrounded by a 14-hectare wooded park in central Melbourne
More than 800,000 visitors come here each year

queen-victoria-building-sydney.name: Queen Victoria Building
descriptions: This Romanesque-style commercial building was inaugurated in 1898
It was nearly demolished in the 1950s and 1970s
Its stained glass and floor mosaics were restored in the 1980s
It houses one of the finest musical clocks in Australia
The building is named after Queen Victoria, who died in 1901

skytower-auckland.name: Sky Tower
descriptions: At 328 meters, it is the tallest structure in the Southern Hemisphere
Visitors can free-fall from its top
It lights up in different colors for national events
Its construction took only 2.5 years, completed in 1997
It withstands winds of more than 200 km/h and earthquakes

beehive-wellington.name: The Beehive (Parliament of Wellington)
descriptions: Its unique round shape earned it the nickname 'The Beehive'
It houses the offices of the ministers and the Prime Minister
Designed by British architect Basil Spence in 1964
Construction stretched over more than ten years
Its modernist style contrasts sharply with the neighboring Neo-Gothic building

christ-church-cathedral-christchurch.name: Christchurch Cathedral
descriptions: The cathedral was severely damaged by the 2011 earthquake
Its original bell tower collapsed during the earthquake
It had been built over more than forty years, from 1864 to 1904
A temporary cardboard cathedral took over after the earthquake
Rebuilding the original building is still debated today

waitangi-treaty-grounds.name: Waitangi Treaty Grounds
descriptions: The Treaty of Waitangi was signed on February 6, 1840 between the Crown and the Maori
This founding document is considered the birth certificate of New Zealand
Its meaning is still debated between the Maori and English versions
February 6 is celebrated every year as New Zealand's national day
The site preserves a beautifully carved Maori meeting house

eden-park-auckland.name: Eden Park
descriptions: Eden Park is New Zealand's national rugby union stadium
It hosted the Rugby World Cup finals in 1987 and 2011
Its capacity is 50,000 spectators
Built on the site of two former drained swamps
The All Blacks have played some of their most memorable matches here

nan-madol.name: Nan Madol
descriptions: This artificial island city is built on 92 basalt islets
It was the administrative center of the Saudeleur dynasty between 1100 and 1628
It is sometimes called the 'Venice of the Pacific'
Listed as a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 2016
The exact origin of its massive basalt blocks remains a mystery

fiji-parliament-suva.name: Parliament of Fiji
descriptions: Fiji's new parliament opened in 1992
It symbolizes the return to democracy after the 1987 coups
The building stands on a hill overlooking Suva Bay
Fiji has been a republic since 1987, after gaining independence in 1970
Suva is one of the largest cities in Melanesia

sacred-heart-cathedral-suva.name: Sacred Heart Cathedral, Suva
descriptions: It is the largest Catholic cathedral in the Pacific Islands
It was consecrated in 1902 by French Marist missionaries
Its Gothic style contrasts with the surrounding tropical architecture
The interior is decorated with stained glass imported from Europe
It is the seat of the Catholic Archdiocese of Suva

robert-louis-stevenson-museum-apia.name: Robert Louis Stevenson Museum
descriptions: Scottish writer Robert Louis Stevenson lived here from 1890 until his death in 1894
He named his estate 'Vailima,' which means 'five waters' in Samoan
He wrote several of his final works here, including Pacific ballads
The Samoans nicknamed him Tusitala, 'the teller of tales'
His grave lies on top of a nearby hill, as he had wished

notre-dame-cathedrale-papeete.name: Notre-Dame Cathedral of Papeete
descriptions: It is the oldest Catholic church in Papeete, inaugurated in 1875
It was built on the initiative of the Picpus missionaries
Its white facade and square towers dominate downtown Tahiti
The interior holds paintings by a local Tahitian artist
It is dedicated to Our Lady of Peace, the patron saint of Tahiti

port-arthur-tasmania.name: Port Arthur Penal Settlement
descriptions: This penal colony was one of the most feared in the British Empire in the 19th century
It held more than 12,500 convicts between 1833 and 1877
Listed as a UNESCO World Heritage Site for its historical significance
The site includes a ruined church that became a symbol of penance
It is now one of the most visited tourist sites in Australia

st-patricks-cathedral-melbourne.name: St Patrick's Cathedral, Melbourne
descriptions: It is the tallest cathedral in the Southern Hemisphere, with a 103-meter spire
Its construction spanned more than 80 years, from 1858 to 1939
It was designed by Irish architect William Wardell
Its Neo-Gothic style is inspired by medieval European cathedrals
It has hosted the funerals of many Australian public figures
